Place the component on a screen and pass that screen's commands.
Handle the keys in a Switch in OnCommand.
Move the component to a component library when a second app needs it.
commonMistakes: Putting the actions inside the component, which ties it to one screen.
Leaving out a default table, so the Commands schema is unknown.
Hiding admin commands in the bar without protecting the action itself.
Different key spellings between the table and the Switch.
troubleshooting: If OnCommand does not appear, the property type must be Event (enable enhanced component properties in Settings if it is missing).
If Enabled never updates, the Commands table must be a formula on the instance, not a collection built once.
If icons do not show, the Icon column must hold Icon enumeration values and the row needs an icon control bound to ThisItem.Icon.
If the bar is cut off on phones, switch to icon-only mode by width or move rarely used commands to an overflow menu.

faqs.question: How do I create a reusable toolbar in Power Apps?
faqs.answer: Build a component that takes a table of commands as an input property and raises an event with the pressed command's key. Each screen passes its own table and handles the event.

faqs.question: Can a Power Apps component run actions on the screen?
faqs.answer: Yes, through an event (behaviour) property. The component raises the event and the screen's formula for that property runs.

faqs.question: How do I share a component between apps?
faqs.answer: Create it in a component library, publish the library and import the component into each app.

create-a-user-acceptance-test-script.shortDescription: A user acceptance test script for a Power Platform app: scenarios by role, numbered steps with expected results, test data, and a sign-off record.
create-a-user-acceptance-test-script.fullDescription: Acceptance testing proves the solution does the job for the people who will use it. A script turns that into repeatable scenarios, each tied to a requirement, run by real users in the test environment with realistic data, with results and defects recorded so sign-off means something.
create-a-user-acceptance-test-script.problemStatement: UAT is an email saying 'please have a look', testers click around the happy path, and gaps appear in the first week of live use.
whenToUse: Before the first production release of an app or flow
Before significant changes to a live solution
When business sign-off is required
whenNotToUse: Maker-level functional testing, which happens earlier in dev
Automated regression checks, which complement this script but do not replace user sign-off
create-a-user-acceptance-test-script.formulaOrCode:
UAT PLAN: <Solution name>   Version <x.y>   Environment: Test   Window: <dates>
Coordinator: <name>   Sign-off owner: <business owner>   Defects logged in: <list or board>

Entry criteria
  [ ] Solution deployed to Test as managed, same version intended for production
  [ ] Test accounts exist for each role, with the same security roles or list permissions as production
  [ ] Test data loaded (see Test data)   [ ] Flows turned on, connections owned by the service account
  [ ] Emails and Teams posts go to testers, not to real customers or all staff

Roles under test
  Requester     tester: <name>      Approver   tester: <name>      Administrator   tester: <name>

Test data
  3 requests in Draft, 3 Waiting for approval, 2 Approved, 1 Rejected
  1 request over the approval threshold (for the second-level route)
  1 user with no manager set (for the fallback route)
  1 record with the longest realistic text, special characters and an attachment near the size limit

Scenario format
  ID | Requirement | Role | Preconditions | Steps | Expected result | Actual | Pass/Fail | Defect ID

UAT-01  Submit a standard request                       Requirement R1   Role: Requester
  1. Open the app from the Teams tab.                     > Home screen loads within a few seconds, shows your name.
  2. Select New request, complete all required fields.    > Submit stays disabled until required fields are valid.
  3. Attach a 5 MB PDF and submit.                        > Confirmation shows a reference number.
  4. Open My requests.                                    > New request is listed with status Waiting for approval.
  5. Check email.                                         > Confirmation email received with a working link.

UAT-02  Validation and errors                           R2   Requester
  1. Enter an end date before the start date.             > Clear message beside the field, submit blocked.
  2. Enter an amount of 0 and a negative amount.          > Rejected with a message.
  3. Turn off the network, select Submit.                 > Error message, entered data is kept.

UAT-03  Approve and reject                              R3   Approver
  1. Open the approval from the email link.               > The correct request opens.
  2. Approve with a comment.                              > Status becomes Approved, requester is notified, comment recorded.
  3. Reject a second request without a comment.           > Blocked until a comment is entered.

UAT-04  Routing rules                                   R4   Requester + Approver
  1. Submit a request over the threshold.                 > Routed to second-level approver after the first approval.
  2. Submit as the user with no manager.                  > Routed to the fallback approver.

UAT-05  Permissions                                     R5   Requester
  1. Try to open another person's request by link.        > Access denied or not found.
  2. Look for administration screens.                     > Not visible, not reachable.

UAT-06  Reminders and escalation                        R6   Approver
  1. Leave a request waiting past the reminder interval.  > Reminder received once, not repeated every run.

UAT-07  Administration                                  R7   Administrator
  1. Change an approval threshold in settings.            > Next request uses the new value without a redeploy.
  2. Export the request list.                             > File contains all rows and expected columns.

UAT-08  Devices and accessibility                       R8   Any
  1. Repeat UAT-01 on a phone.                            > Usable without horizontal scrolling.
  2. Complete the form with keyboard only.                > Every field and button reachable in a sensible order.

Defect severity
  1 Blocks the process, no workaround     must fix before sign-off
  2 Wrong result, workaround exists       fix before go-live unless the owner accepts in writing
  3 Cosmetic or wording                   schedule

Exit criteria
  [ ] All scenarios run   [ ] No open severity 1 or 2 defects   [ ] Fixed defects retested, related scenarios re-run
  [ ] Accepted exceptions listed with owner

Sign-off
  I confirm version <x.y> was tested against this script and is accepted for production.
  Name / Role / Date     Known exceptions: <list or none>
stepByStepInstructions: List the requirements and map at least one scenario to each.
Write scenarios per role with numbered steps and expected results.
Prepare test accounts and test data in the test environment.
Brief the testers and agree the test window.
Run the scenarios, record actual results and log defects.
Fix, redeploy the solution and retest affected scenarios.
Collect written sign-off against a specific version.
commonMistakes: Testing in the development environment with maker permissions.
Scenarios with no expected result, so pass or fail is opinion.
Only testing the happy path and never errors, permissions or routing.
Signing off a version that is then changed before release.
troubleshooting: If testers cannot open the app, share it and assign the security role or list permission in the test environment.
If flows do not run during UAT, they are off after import or their connections are not set. Check the solution's flows and connection references.
If results differ between testers, their roles differ. Record the account used for each scenario.
If defects keep reappearing, fixes are being made in Test. Fix in Dev and redeploy.

faqs.question: What should a Power Apps UAT script include?
faqs.answer: Entry criteria, roles and test accounts, test data, scenarios with steps and expected results mapped to requirements, defect severities, exit criteria and a sign-off record for a named version.

faqs.question: Who should run user acceptance tests?
faqs.answer: People who will use the solution in each role, using test accounts with production-like permissions. Makers should not sign off their own work.

faqs.question: Which environment should UAT run in?
faqs.answer: A separate test environment holding the managed solution that will go to production, with test data and notifications pointed at the testers.

create-a-production-support-guide.shortDescription: A support guide for a live Power Platform solution: who owns it, how it is built, common problems with their fixes, and how to escalate.
create-a-production-support-guide.fullDescription: When the maker is on holiday and the app stops working, the person who picks up the call needs one document that says what the solution is, where its parts live, what usually goes wrong and what they are allowed to do about it. Writing this before go-live is the difference between a ten-minute fix and a two-day outage.
create-a-production-support-guide.problemStatement: Support knowledge lives in one maker's head. When something breaks, nobody knows which flow, which list, which account or who to call.
whenToUse: Every solution that the business depends on
Handing a solution from a project team to operations
Solutions run by a service account
whenNotToUse: Personal productivity apps with one user
Proofs of concept that will be rebuilt before release
create-a-production-support-guide.formulaOrCode:
SUPPORT GUIDE: <Solution name>          Last reviewed: <date>   Review every 6 months and after each release

1. Summary
  What it does (two sentences):
  Users: <who, how many>            Business owner: <name>          Criticality: High / Medium / Low
  Support hours: <hours>            Target response: <for example 4 working hours>

2. Contacts
  First line (service desk):   <queue>
  Second line (app support):   <team or names>
  Maker / technical owner:     <name>      Backup: <name>
  Business owner:              <name>      Platform admin team: <contact>

3. What it is made of
  Environment:   <Prod name and URL>        Solution: <name>, managed, version <x.y>
  Apps:          <name> (canvas / model-driven), link: <URL>
  Flows:         <name> | trigger | what it does | owner
  Data:          <SharePoint site and lists / Dataverse tables>
  Connections:   <connector> | account used | connection reference name
  Service account: <svc account>  licence: <type>   password and MFA held by: <team, vault>
  Environment variables: <name> | purpose | current value location
  Security:      <groups or security roles> | who approves access
  Dependencies:  <other systems, APIs, gateways>

4. Routine tasks
  Add a user:            add to group <name> (owner approval required)
  Change reference data: edit list <name> / settings screen in the app
  Check health:          Power Automate > Solutions > <solution> > Cloud flows > 28-day run history
  Licence and capacity:  <where to check>

5. Known problems and fixes
  Symptom: "You need permission to access this item" on opening the app
    Cause: user not in the access group or missing list permission
    Fix: add to <group>; allow up to an hour for the change to apply
  Symptom: requests stuck in "Waiting for approval"
    Cause: approval flow failed or is turned off
    Fix: open the flow's run history, read the failed action, resubmit the run after fixing the cause
  Symptom: flow fails with 401 or "connection is not configured"
    Cause: service account password changed or connection expired
    Fix: sign in again on the connection as the service account (Connections > Fix connection)
  Symptom: flow fails with 429 or runs slowly
    Cause: throttling
    Fix: wait for retry; check for a loop or a bulk import; reduce concurrency
  Symptom: gallery missing recent or older records
    Cause: delegation limit or a filter view
    Fix: report to the maker with an example record
  Symptom: emails not arriving
    Cause: sender mailbox, quota or recipient rule
    Fix: check the run output for the Send email action, then the mailbox's sent items

6. What support may do without asking
  Resubmit failed runs      Fix a connection as the service account      Add or remove users with owner approval
  Turn a flow off in an incident (tell the owner)

7. What needs the maker or a change request
  Editing apps or flows in production (managed solutions should be changed in Dev and redeployed)
  Changing columns, tables or permissions models      Deleting data

8. Incident steps
  1. Confirm scope: one user or everyone? Since when? What changed?
  2. Check Microsoft 365 service health and the environment's status.
  3. Check flow run history and the app's Monitor session if the user can reproduce.
  4. Apply a known fix or escalate with: time, user, screenshot, run link, error text.
  5. Tell the business owner and users what to do meanwhile.
  6. Record cause and fix in section 5.

9. Recovery
  Data restore:    SharePoint recycle bin (93 days) / version history; Dataverse environment backup (admin centre)
  Solution rollback: import the previous managed version (kept at <location>) or redeploy from source control
  Manual fallback: <how the process runs without the app, form or email address>

10. Change history
  Date | Version | Change | By
stepByStepInstructions: Fill in ownership, contacts and criticality with the business owner.
Inventory apps, flows, data, connections and accounts.
Write the routine tasks support will be asked for.
Record known problems with cause and fix, starting from test and pilot issues.
Define what support may change and what needs the maker.
Add recovery and manual fallback steps.
Store the guide with the solution and review it after every release and incident.
commonMistakes: Writing the guide after the first incident.
Listing people without a backup.
Leaving out which account each connection uses.
Letting support edit managed flows directly in production.
troubleshooting: If nobody knows the owner of a flow, check the solution's flow details and the environment inventory, then record it in the guide.
If the service account's credentials cannot be found, they were never vaulted. Reset them with the identity team and re-authenticate connections.
If the guide is out of date, tie its review to the release checklist.
If support has no access to run history, add the support group as flow co-owners or give them an environment role that can view it.

faqs.question: What should a Power Apps support document contain?
faqs.answer: Ownership and contacts, an inventory of apps, flows, data and connections, routine tasks, known problems with fixes, what support may change, incident steps and recovery options.

faqs.question: Who should support a Power Platform solution in production?
faqs.answer: A named team with a backup, not a single maker. The service desk handles access and known fixes, and the maker or platform team handles changes.

faqs.question: How do I roll back a Power Platform release?
faqs.answer: Keep the previous managed solution version and import it again, or redeploy the earlier build from source control. Data changes need their own restore plan.

create-a-release-notes-panel.shortDescription: Show users what changed in the latest version of a canvas app: a release notes list, a panel that opens once per version, and a link to reopen it.
create-a-release-notes-panel.fullDescription: Users notice when a button moves but rarely read the email about it. A small panel inside the app that appears once after each release, lists the changes in plain words and can be reopened from the menu gets the message to people at the moment they need it.
create-a-release-notes-panel.problemStatement: A new version is published, users are surprised by changes, and the support desk gets the same three questions for a week.
whenToUse: Apps with regular releases and a broad user base
Changes that alter how a task is done
When release communication should be recorded
whenNotToUse: Bug-fix releases with nothing visible to users
Apps with a handful of users who were part of the change
stepByStepInstructions: Create the release notes list and add an entry for the current version.
Create the views list with an indexed email column.
Add named formulas for the app name and latest published release.
Build the panel and show it when the user has no view record for the latest version.
Record the view when the user dismisses the panel.
Add a version label and a link to reopen the notes.
Publish a notes entry as part of every release.
commonMistakes: Showing the panel on every launch.
Writing notes in technical language or ticket references.
Blocking the app when the view record cannot be saved.
Publishing the notes entry before the new version is live.
troubleshooting: If the panel never appears, check that the notes entry is marked published and AppName matches exactly.
If it appears every time, the Patch to the views list is failing. Check the user's permission to add items.
If changes show as one long line, the Changes field must be plain text with one change per line.
If users on shared devices see the wrong state with SaveData, use the list approach, which is per user.

faqs.question: How do I show a what's new message in Power Apps?
faqs.answer: Keep release notes in a list, look up the latest published entry and show a panel when the current user has no record of seeing that version.

faqs.question: How do I show a popup only once per user?
faqs.answer: Write a row with the user's email and the version when they dismiss it, and check for that row before showing the panel.

faqs.question: Where should the app version number come from?
faqs.answer: From the latest published release notes entry, so the label and the notes always agree.

create-a-department-request-site.shortDescription: Set up a SharePoint site where a department takes in requests: a request list with the right columns, views per audience, a form, and a simple notification flow.
create-a-department-request-site.fullDescription: Most departments start taking requests by email and a spreadsheet. A small SharePoint site replaces both: one list holds every request with status, owner and dates, views show each audience what they need, and a flow acknowledges and routes new items. It is the simplest useful intake system and a good base for a Power App later.
create-a-department-request-site.problemStatement: Requests arrive by email, chat and corridor conversation. Nobody can say how many are open, who owns them or how long they take.
whenToUse: A team such as HR, facilities, finance or IT that receives regular requests
Volumes from a few a week to a few hundred a month
When a ticketing product would be more than the team needs
whenNotToUse: Requests containing data that needs record-level security beyond SharePoint's item permissions
High-volume service desks with service levels, queues and knowledge bases, which need a service management tool
create-a-department-request-site.formulaOrCode:
Site
  Type: Team site (no Microsoft 365 group needed) or Communication site if most visitors only submit
  Name: <Department> Requests        URL: /sites/<dept>-requests
  Permissions:
    Owners   2 named people from the department
    Members  the team that works requests (Edit)
    Visitors everyone who may submit: grant "Contribute" on the Requests list only, or collect through a form

List: Requests
  Title                  Single line     "Short summary"            required
  RequestType            Choice          Access | Equipment | Information | Change | Other      required, indexed
  Details                Multiple lines  plain text
  Priority               Choice          Low | Normal | High         default Normal
  Status                 Choice          New | In progress | Waiting on requester | Done | Declined   default New, indexed
  AssignedTo             Person          single
  NeededBy               Date
  RequesterDepartment    Choice or managed metadata
  ResolutionNotes        Multiple lines  plain text
  ClosedOn               Date and time
  (Created By and Created give requester and submission time)
  Versioning on. Attachments on if evidence is needed.

Item-level visibility (optional)
  List settings > Advanced settings > Item-level permissions:
    Read access: items that were created by the user      Edit: items that were created by the user
  Team members need "Manage Lists" or "Override list behaviors" permission to see everything.
  This setting is a convenience, not strong security.

Views
  My requests        Created By = [Me], sort Created descending                     (default for visitors)
  New and unassigned Status = New, AssignedTo is empty, sort Created ascending
  My work            AssignedTo = [Me], Status <> Done and <> Declined
  Open by type       Status not Done/Declined, group by RequestType
  Overdue            NeededBy < [Today], Status not Done/Declined
  Closed this month  Status = Done, ClosedOn >= start of month (filter: ClosedOn >= [Today]-30)

Form
  List > New > Edit form > Edit columns: show Title, RequestType, Details, NeededBy, Priority only.
  Hide Status, AssignedTo, ResolutionNotes and ClosedOn from requesters.
  Conditional field example (Configure layout or column conditional formula):
    Show NeededBy only for Equipment:   =if([$RequestType] == 'Equipment', 'true', 'false')
  Or use a Microsoft List form (Forms button on the list) to collect requests without giving list access.

Status formatting (Column settings > Format this column > Choice pills) for Status and Priority.

Flow: When an item is created (Requests)
  1. Send an email (V2) to the requester:  "We received your request: <Title>. Reference: <ID>."
  2. Switch on RequestType: set AssignedTo to the type's owner (keep owners in a small "Request Owners" list)
  3. Post a message in the team's Teams channel with a link to the item
Flow: When an item is modified, trigger condition on Status = Done
  @equals(triggerOutputs()?['body/Status/Value'], 'Done')
  1. Update item: ClosedOn = utcNow()   (guard against loops with the trigger condition)
  2. Email the requester with ResolutionNotes

Home page
  Button "Submit a request" linking to the new item form:  <site>/Lists/Requests/NewForm.aspx
  List web part filtered to "My requests"      Text web part: what to expect and response times

Measures to review monthly
  Requests opened and closed, open by type, average days from Created to ClosedOn, overdue count.
stepByStepInstructions: Create the site and set owners, members and who may submit.
Build the Requests list with the columns above and index Status and RequestType.
Create the views for requesters and for the team.
Trim the new item form to the fields a requester should fill in.
Add the acknowledgement and routing flow.
Add the close-out flow with a trigger condition.
Build a home page with a submit button and a My requests view.
commonMistakes: Asking requesters to fill in status and owner fields.
Giving every visitor edit rights to the whole site.
No view for unassigned items, so new requests sit unseen.
Free-text request types that cannot be grouped or routed.
troubleshooting: If requesters cannot submit, they need at least Contribute on the list, or use a list form link.
If team members cannot see items after turning on item-level permissions, give them a permission level that includes Override list behaviors.
If the close-out flow runs repeatedly, add the trigger condition so it fires only when Status is Done and ClosedOn is empty.
If the Overdue view shows a threshold error on a large list, index NeededBy and Status.

faqs.question: How do I create a request system in SharePoint?
faqs.answer: Create a list with type, status, owner and date columns, add views for requesters and the team, simplify the new item form and use a flow to acknowledge and route new items.

faqs.question: Can users see only their own requests in a SharePoint list?
faqs.answer: Yes. Item-level permissions in the list's advanced settings limit reading and editing to items the user created. It is a convenience setting, not strong security.

faqs.question: When should I use a Power App for requests?
faqs.answer: When the form needs logic the list form cannot provide, such as multi-step screens, lookups across lists or role-based layouts. The same list can stay as the data source.

create-a-controlled-document-workspace.shortDescription: A SharePoint library for controlled documents such as policies and procedures: draft and published versions, approval, document numbers, review dates and a read-only published view.
create-a-controlled-document-workspace.fullDescription: Controlled documents have rules: one current approved version, a record of who approved it and when, a review date, and no editing of the published copy. A SharePoint library with major and minor versioning, content approval, required metadata and tight permissions meets these rules without extra software.
create-a-controlled-document-workspace.problemStatement: Policies live in shared folders as 'Final v3 (2).docx'. Staff cannot tell which version is current, and audits ask for approval evidence nobody can find.
whenToUse: Policies, procedures, work instructions and quality documents
Teams audited against standards such as ISO 9001 or similar
When staff must only ever see the approved version
whenNotToUse: Everyday collaboration files, where this much control slows people down
Regulated records needing formal retention and disposition, which also need Microsoft Purview
create-a-controlled-document-workspace.formulaOrCode:
Site
  Dedicated site, for example /sites/policies. Do not mix with a team's working files.
  Groups:   Document Controllers (Full control or Edit + Approve)
            Authors (Contribute)        Approvers (Approve permission level)        All staff (Read)

Library: Controlled Documents
  Library settings > Versioning settings
    Require content approval for submitted items:     Yes
    Document version history:                         Create major and minor (draft) versions
    Keep major versions: 50     Keep drafts for: 5 major versions
    Draft item security:                              Only users who can approve items (and the author)
    Require check out:                                Yes
  Result: readers see only the last approved major version (1.0, 2.0). Drafts (1.1, 1.2) are hidden from them.

Columns (via a "Controlled Document" content type so they travel with the template)
  DocumentNumber     Single line, enforce unique values       for example POL-HR-012
  DocumentType       Choice     Policy | Procedure | Work instruction | Form | Standard         required
  OwningDepartment   Managed metadata or choice                                                  required
  DocumentOwner      Person                                                                      required
  Approver           Person
  EffectiveDate      Date
  NextReviewDate     Date        indexed                                                         required
  ReviewCycleMonths  Number      default 12
  Status             Choice     Draft | In review | Approved | Superseded | Withdrawn
  ChangeSummary      Multiple lines     what changed in this version
  Supersedes         Single line        number of the document this one replaces

Numbering
  <TYPE>-<DEPT>-<3 digits>     POL-HR-012, PRO-FIN-004
  Keep the next number per type and department in a small "Document Numbers" list, issued by a flow,
  so two authors never take the same number.

Lifecycle
  1. Author uploads or creates from the template  > version 0.1, Status Draft
  2. Author checks in and edits                   > 0.2, 0.3 ...
  3. Author publishes a major version             > approval status Pending
  4. Approver approves                            > 1.0 visible to all staff
  5. Changes start again as 1.1 while readers continue to see 1.0
  6. Approved revision becomes 2.0

Approval flow (When a file is created or modified, properties only; trigger condition on Pending)
  @equals(triggerOutputs()?['body/{ModerationStatus}'], 'Pending')
  1. Start and wait for an approval, assigned to the Approver column, with a link and ChangeSummary
  2. If approved:  Set content approval status = Approved (needs the ETag from Get file properties)
                   Update file properties: Status = Approved, EffectiveDate = today,
                   NextReviewDate = addToTime(utcNow(), ReviewCycleMonths, 'Month')
  3. If rejected:  Set content approval status = Rejected with the approver's comments; email the author

Review reminder flow (Recurrence, weekly)
  Get files (properties only), filter query:
    NextReviewDate le '@{addDays(utcNow(), 60)}' and Status eq 'Approved'
  Email each DocumentOwner one message listing their documents due for review.

Views
  Published (default for staff)   Status = Approved, columns: Number, Name, Type, Department, Effective, Next review
  My drafts                       Created By or Modified By = [Me], Approval Status <> Approved
  Awaiting approval               Approval Status = Pending
  Review due                      NextReviewDate <= [Today]+60, Status = Approved
  Superseded and withdrawn        for controllers only (audience targeting or a separate view)

Reader experience
  Link staff to the Published view or a page with a filtered library web part, never to folders.
  Turn on "Open in browser" so readers do not download copies.
  Add a header or footer field in the Word template bound to DocumentNumber and version label:
    Insert > Quick Parts > Document Property > DocumentNumber / Label.

Withdrawing a document
  Set Status = Withdrawn, then unpublish the major version (or move to an archive library readers cannot see).
  Keep it. Auditors ask for the version that was in force on a past date.
stepByStepInstructions: Create a dedicated site with controller, author, approver and reader groups.
Turn on content approval, major and minor versions and required check-out.
Add the controlled document content type and columns.
Set up document numbering.
Build the approval flow that sets approval status and review dates.
Add the review reminder flow.
Create the published view and point staff to it.
commonMistakes: Leaving draft visibility open so readers see unapproved versions.
Giving authors the Approve permission.
No review date, so documents are never revisited.
Deleting superseded documents that auditors later request.
troubleshooting: If readers see drafts, set Draft item security to only users who can approve items.
If Set content approval status fails, pass the current ETag from Get file properties and make sure the flow account can approve.
If the approval flow triggers itself, use the trigger condition on Pending and avoid editing properties while the status is Pending.
If the document number shows blank in Word, the template must come from the content type so the property is bound.

faqs.question: How do I manage controlled documents in SharePoint?
faqs.answer: Use a library with content approval, major and minor versioning and required check-out, add metadata for number, owner and review date, and restrict who can approve.

faqs.question: How do I make sure users only see the approved version?
faqs.answer: Turn on content approval and set draft item security to approvers and authors only. Readers then see the last approved major version.

faqs.question: How do I remind owners to review documents?
faqs.answer: Store a next review date on each document and run a scheduled flow that emails owners a list of documents due in the next 60 days.

create-a-site-owner-review-process.shortDescription: A recurring review in which every SharePoint site's owners confirm the site is still needed, its owners are right and its sharing is appropriate.
create-a-site-owner-review-process.fullDescription: Sites outlive their projects and their owners. A scheduled attestation asks each site's owners a few direct questions, records the answers, chases non-responders and escalates sites with no reply. It keeps ownership current and feeds the archive process with sites nobody claims.
create-a-site-owner-review-process.problemStatement: The tenant has thousands of sites. Many have one owner who has left, external guests nobody remembers inviting, and content nobody will vouch for.
whenToUse: Tenants with self-service site or team creation
Organisations with external sharing enabled
As the first step of lifecycle and archive management
whenNotToUse: Tenants with a few dozen centrally managed sites, where a manual check is quicker
Where Microsoft 365 group expiration and access reviews in Entra ID already cover every site in scope
create-a-site-owner-review-process.formulaOrCode:
What owners are asked (twice a year, or yearly for low-risk sites)
  1. Is this site still needed?                    Yes / No, archive it / No, delete it
  2. Are the listed owners correct?                Yes / No (name the right owners)
  3. Are the members and guests still appropriate? Yes / I have removed those who no longer need access
  4. Does the site hold sensitive information?     Yes / No
  A site needs at least two owners who are current employees.

Register: list "Site Reviews" in an admin site
  Title (site name)        SiteUrl (hyperlink or text, indexed)      SiteId (text)
  Owners (person, multi)   Template (text)        Sensitivity (text)        ExternalSharing (text)
  StorageUsedGB (number)   LastActivity (date)    GuestCount (number)
  ReviewCycle (text, for example 2026-H2)          ReviewStatus (choice: Not sent | Sent | Confirmed | Changes requested |
                                                    No response | Archive requested)
  SentOn (date)   RespondedOn (date)   RespondedBy (person)   Response (multiple lines)   RemindersSent (number)

Load the register (PnP PowerShell, run by a SharePoint admin)
  Connect-PnPOnline -Url https://contoso-admin.sharepoint.com -Interactive
  $sites = Get-PnPTenantSite -Detailed | Where-Object { $_.Template -notlike "SPSPERS*" -and $_.Template -ne "APPCATALOG#0" }
  foreach ($s in $sites) {
      [pscustomobject]@{
          Title = $s.Title; SiteUrl = $s.Url; Template = $s.Template
          StorageUsedGB = [math]::Round($s.StorageUsageCurrent / 1024, 2)
          LastActivity = $s.LastContentModifiedDate; ExternalSharing = $s.SharingCapability
          Sensitivity = $s.SensitivityLabel; Owner = $s.OwnerLoginName; GroupId = $s.GroupId
      }
  } | Export-Csv .\sites.csv -NoTypeInformation
  # Group-connected sites: owners come from the group
  #   Get-PnPMicrosoft365GroupOwner -Identity <GroupId>
  # Then add or update rows in "Site Reviews" (Add-PnPListItem / Set-PnPListItem) with ReviewCycle set.

Flow 1: send review requests (manual or scheduled at the start of the cycle)
  Get items: ReviewStatus eq 'Not sent' and ReviewCycle eq '2026-H2'
  Apply to each (concurrency 5):
    Post adaptive card and wait for a response (Teams) to each owner, or Start and wait for an approval
    with custom responses "Still needed", "Archive it", "Owners need changing".
    Card shows: site name and link, current owners, guest count, last activity, storage.
    Update item: ReviewStatus = Sent, SentOn = utcNow()
  Simpler option: email a link to the item's edit form with only the response fields shown.

Flow 2: record the response
  On response: ReviewStatus = Confirmed | Changes requested | Archive requested, RespondedOn, RespondedBy, Response.
  "Changes requested" creates a task for the admin team. "Archive requested" feeds the archive process.

Flow 3: reminders and escalation (Recurrence, weekly)
  Sent more than 14 days ago, no response, RemindersSent < 2    > remind owners, RemindersSent + 1
  Sent more than 35 days ago, no response                       > ReviewStatus = No response,
                                                                  notify the owners' managers and the admin team
  No response after a further 30 days                           > make the site read-only and post a banner
     Set-PnPTenantSite -Identity <url> -LockState ReadOnly
     (reverse with -LockState Unlock). Agree this step with the business before the first cycle.

Sites with no valid owner
  Owners all disabled or deleted: assign the last active member's manager or the department head, record the decision.

Report at the end of each cycle
  Sites reviewed, confirmed, changed, archived, no response; guests removed; storage released.

Built-in features to combine with this
  Microsoft 365 group expiration policy (Entra ID): owners renew the group or it is deleted (soft delete 30 days).
  Entra access reviews for guests: owners confirm guest access periodically.
  SharePoint Advanced Management: site lifecycle and ownership policies, where licensed.
stepByStepInstructions: Agree the questions, cycle and what happens to sites with no response.
Create the Site Reviews register.
Export sites and owners with PnP PowerShell and load the register.
Build the flow that sends the review to each site's owners.
Record responses and create tasks for requested changes.
Add reminders, escalation and the read-only step.
Report results and start the next cycle from the same register.
commonMistakes: Sending a long questionnaire that owners ignore.
No consequence for not responding.
Emailing only the primary site collection admin and missing group owners.
Locking sites without warning or business agreement.
troubleshooting: If owners are blank for group-connected sites, read owners from the Microsoft 365 group, not the site.
If Teams cards fail for some owners, the account is disabled or unlicensed. Route those sites to the no-valid-owner path.
If the flow is throttled sending thousands of cards, send in batches by department over several days.
If a locked site is needed urgently, unlock it with Set-PnPTenantSite and record who asked.

faqs.question: How do I find out who owns each SharePoint site?
faqs.answer: Use Get-PnPTenantSite for the site list and, for group-connected sites, read the owners of the Microsoft 365 group. Record them in a register.

faqs.question: How often should site owners review their sites?
faqs.answer: Once or twice a year for most sites, and more often for sites with external guests or sensitive content.

faqs.question: What should happen if no owner responds?
faqs.answer: Remind, escalate to managers, then make the site read-only after a published deadline, and pass it to the archive process if still unclaimed.

create-a-lifecycle-archive-process.shortDescription: Archive SharePoint sites that are finished or unclaimed: criteria, owner notice, a read-only period, then Microsoft 365 Archive or deletion, with a register of every decision.
create-a-lifecycle-archive-process.fullDescription: Old sites cost storage, clutter search and keep sharing links alive. An archive process gives each site a clear end: it is identified by agreed criteria, its owners are told, it is made read-only for a period, and then it is archived or deleted in line with retention rules. Every step is recorded and reversible until the final one.
create-a-lifecycle-archive-process.problemStatement: Nobody deletes anything because nobody is sure it is safe, so storage grows every year and search returns ten-year-old project files.
whenToUse: Tenants approaching their storage quota
After projects close or a site review finds unclaimed sites
When old content is surfacing in search or Copilot answers
whenNotToUse: Sites under legal hold or active retention policies that prevent deletion
Active sites that are simply large, which need clean-up inside the site instead
create-a-lifecycle-archive-process.formulaOrCode:
Criteria (a site is a candidate when any of these is true)
  Owner requested archive in the site review
  No content modified and no page views for 12 months (LastContentModifiedDate + usage reports)
  Project or contract end date passed by 6 months
  No valid owner after the escalation steps

Stages and timings
  Stage 0  Candidate         added to the register with the reason
  Stage 1  Notice            owners and members told; 30 days to object
  Stage 2  Read-only         site locked, banner added; 60 days
  Stage 3  Archived          moved to Microsoft 365 Archive (cold storage), or kept read-only if Archive is not licensed
  Stage 4  Deleted           after the retention period for its content, if policy allows; recycle bin 93 days

Register: "Site Archive Register"
  SiteUrl | Title | Owners | Reason | Stage | NoticeSentOn | LockedOn | ArchivedOn | DeletedOn |
  RetentionCategory | EarliestDeleteDate | ApprovedBy | Notes | StorageGB

Checks before stage 2
  [ ] No legal hold or eDiscovery case includes the site (ask compliance)
  [ ] Retention labels and policies reviewed: note the earliest permitted deletion date
  [ ] No live flows, Power Apps or Power BI datasets depend on lists or files in the site
  [ ] No other sites link to it as a hub, or the hub association is removed
  [ ] Owners have had the chance to move anything still needed

Notice text (stage 1)
  Subject: <Site name> will be archived on <date>
  This site has had no activity since <date>. It will become read-only on <date> and be archived on <date>.
  If it is still needed, reply or select "Keep this site" by <date>. Nothing is deleted at this stage.

Commands (PnP PowerShell, SharePoint admin)
  # Stage 2: read-only
  Set-PnPTenantSite -Identity $url -LockState ReadOnly
  # Stop new sharing and hide from search
  Set-PnPTenantSite -Identity $url -SharingCapability Disabled
  Connect-PnPOnline -Url $url -Interactive; Set-PnPWeb -NoCrawl:$true     # or Set-PnPSite -NoCrawl in older modules

  # Stage 3: Microsoft 365 Archive (must be enabled for the tenant; billed per GB at a lower rate)
  Set-PnPTenantSite -Identity $url -LockState Unlock
  Set-SPOSite -Identity $url -ArchiveState Archived          # SharePoint Online Management Shell
  # Reactivate:  Set-SPOSite -Identity $url -ArchiveState Active
  # Reactivation is immediate within 7 days and can take up to 24 hours later; a reactivation fee may apply.

  # Group-connected sites and teams
  # Archive the team in Teams first (Teams admin centre or Set-TeamArchivedState), which makes the site read-only
  # for members, then archive the site.

  # Stage 4: delete
  Remove-PnPTenantSite -Url $url          # goes to the site recycle bin for 93 days
  # Group-connected: delete the Microsoft 365 group (soft-deleted 30 days, site retained 93)
  # Restore: Restore-PnPTenantRecycleBinItem -Url $url

Banner for read-only sites
  The lock already shows "This site is read-only at the administrator's request."
  Add who to contact in the site's description or a page header before locking.

Flow to drive the stages (Recurrence, daily)
  Stage = Notice and NoticeSentOn older than 30 days, no objection  > create an admin task "Lock <site>"
  Stage = Read-only and LockedOn older than 60 days                 > task "Archive <site>"
  Stage = Archived and EarliestDeleteDate reached                   > task "Review for deletion", needs approval
  Keep the tenant-level commands with admins; the flow tracks dates and raises tasks.

Requests to bring a site back
  Record who asked and why, reactivate, set a new owner pair, and put the site back in the review cycle.

Report quarterly
  Sites archived and deleted, storage released, reactivations, objections.
stepByStepInstructions: Agree criteria, stages and timings with records and compliance teams.
Create the archive register.
Identify candidates from the site review and activity reports.
Run the pre-lock checks, then send notice to owners and members.
Lock the site read-only and remove it from search and sharing.
Archive with Microsoft 365 Archive or keep read-only.
Delete only when retention allows, with approval, and record it.
commonMistakes: Deleting sites that hold content under a retention policy or hold.
Archiving a site that a live flow or app still uses.
Skipping the read-only period, so problems appear only after deletion.
No route for bringing a site back.
troubleshooting: If the archive command fails, Microsoft 365 Archive is not enabled or the site is locked. Unlock it first.
If a site cannot be deleted, a retention policy or hold applies. Leave it archived and record the earliest delete date.
If users report a broken app after a lock, a flow or app writes to the site. Unlock, move the dependency, then lock again.
If archived content still appears in search for a while, the index takes time to update after NoCrawl or archiving.

faqs.question: How do I archive a SharePoint site?
faqs.answer: Make it read-only, tell its owners, then use Microsoft 365 Archive to move it to cold storage, or keep it locked if Archive is not available. Record each step.

faqs.question: What is the difference between archiving and deleting a site?
faqs.answer: An archived site is kept in lower-cost storage and can be reactivated. A deleted site stays in the recycle bin for 93 days and is then gone unless retention keeps a copy.

faqs.question: Can I delete a site that has a retention policy?
faqs.answer: Not until the retention period ends. Check policies and holds before any deletion.

create-a-document-retention-checklist.shortDescription: A checklist for applying retention to a SharePoint library: decide what the records are, map them to retention labels, publish and apply the labels, and prove it works.
create-a-document-retention-checklist.fullDescription: Retention decides how long documents are kept and what happens afterwards. In Microsoft 365 that is done with Purview retention labels and policies, not with flows that delete files. This checklist walks a site owner and a records manager through the decisions and settings for one library, from schedule to evidence.
create-a-document-retention-checklist.problemStatement: Documents are kept forever because nobody decided otherwise, or deleted by a home-made flow with no record, and neither position survives an audit.
whenToUse: Libraries holding contracts, HR, finance, project or quality records
Before migrating or archiving content
When a regulator or auditor asks how long records are kept
whenNotToUse: Working files with no retention requirement beyond a tenant-wide default policy
Tenants without the licences for retention labels, where only basic policies are available
create-a-document-retention-checklist.formulaOrCode:
1. Decide (site owner + records manager)
  [ ] List the record types in the library:  for example Signed contract, Invoice, Meeting notes
  [ ] For each: retention period, what starts the clock, what happens at the end, and the source of the rule

  Record type       Keep for    Clock starts            At the end              Source
  Signed contract   7 years     contract end date       disposition review      company policy FIN-07
  Invoice           7 years     created                 delete automatically    tax law
  Project minutes   3 years     last modified           delete automatically    project standard
  Policy document   permanent   n/a                     keep (record)           quality manual

  [ ] Anything that must never be edited after declaration? (mark the label as a record)
  [ ] Who reviews disposition? (named people, not one person)

2. Create labels (Microsoft Purview portal > Records management or Data lifecycle management > Labels)
  [ ] One label per row above, named so users understand it:  "Contract - 7 years after end"
  [ ] Retain items for <period>, starting from: created / last modified / labelled / an event
  [ ] Event-based (contract end): create an event type "Contract end"; the library needs an Asset ID or
      contract number column mapped to the event
  [ ] End action: delete automatically / start a disposition review / do nothing
  [ ] Record or regulatory record only where required (regulatory record cannot be removed, even by admins)

3. Publish (Label policies > Publish labels)
  [ ] Publish to the specific sites or to an adaptive scope, not the whole tenant by default
  [ ] Allow up to 7 days for labels to appear in the site (usually within a day)

4. Apply in the library
  [ ] Default label:  Library settings > Apply label to items in this list or library > choose the label
      (applies to new items; tick the option to apply to existing items if that is intended)
  [ ] Or by folder or document set: Details pane > Apply label
  [ ] Or by content type or metadata with an auto-apply policy (E5 or equivalent licence):
      condition example   ContentType:"Signed Contract"   or a sensitive information type
  [ ] Add the "Retention label" and "Label applied by" columns to a view
  [ ] Add the column the retention period depends on (ContractEndDate) and make it required

5. Check
  [ ] View: group by Retention label; filter for items with no label
  [ ] Try to delete a labelled item: blocked for records; for non-record labels the copy is kept in the
      Preservation Hold library until the period ends
  [ ] Records: confirm the lock icon and that editing is blocked or versioned as designed
  [ ] Trigger a test event for event-based labels and confirm the expiry date on an item
  [ ] Content explorer / activity explorer in Purview shows labelled counts for the site

6. Disposition
  [ ] Disposition reviewers receive the notification and can approve, extend or relabel
  [ ] Proof of disposition is retained (Purview keeps it for up to 7 years)
  [ ] A calendar reminder exists for the first expected disposition date

7. Guardrails
  [ ] No flows or scripts delete documents in this library
  [ ] Site archive or deletion plans checked against the labels (a labelled site cannot simply be deleted)
  [ ] Legal holds override retention: confirm with legal before any bulk action
  [ ] Version history limits reviewed, since versions count toward storage for the whole period
  [ ] Owners know that moving a file out of the library can change its default label

8. Record the set-up
  Library | Label | Period | Trigger | End action | Reviewers | Policy name | Date applied | Approved by
stepByStepInstructions: List the record types in the library with period, trigger and end action.
Create a retention label for each in Microsoft Purview.
Publish the labels to the site.
Set a default label on the library or apply labels by folder or content type.
Add retention columns to a view and find unlabelled items.
Test deletion, record locking and disposition.
Record the configuration and who approved it.
commonMistakes: Using a flow to delete old files in place of retention labels.
Publishing every label to every site.
Choosing 'when created' as the trigger for contracts that run for years.
Marking everything as a regulatory record, which cannot be undone.
troubleshooting: If labels do not appear in the library, the policy has not finished distributing or the site is not in its scope.
If a default label did not apply to existing files, re-save the setting with the existing items option, and allow time for processing.
If users cannot delete a file, it is a record or under hold. That is the label working.
If storage grows after applying labels, deleted and edited copies are being kept in the Preservation Hold library for the period.

faqs.question: How do I set a retention period on a SharePoint library?
faqs.answer: Create a retention label in Microsoft Purview, publish it to the site, then set it as the library's default label in library settings.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a retention policy and a retention label?
faqs.answer: A policy applies one rule to whole locations such as all sites. A label applies to individual items or libraries and supports records, event-based periods and disposition review.

faqs.question: Should I use Power Automate to delete old documents?
faqs.answer: No, not for records. Retention labels keep an auditable history and respect holds. A flow that deletes files has neither.

create-a-page-quality-audit.shortDescription: Audit the pages of a SharePoint intranet site against a short quality standard: ownership, freshness, accuracy, links, accessibility and findability.
create-a-page-quality-audit.fullDescription: Intranet pages decay quietly. A page audit lists every page with its owner, last modified date and views, scores each against a few objective checks, and gives owners a short list of fixes. Run twice a year, it keeps the site trustworthy and gives search and Copilot better material to work from.
create-a-page-quality-audit.problemStatement: The intranet has hundreds of pages. Some are years out of date, some have no owner, and staff have stopped trusting what they find.
whenToUse: Communication sites and intranets with many authors
Before a redesign, migration or Copilot rollout
As a regular content governance cycle
whenNotToUse: Team sites where pages are incidental to files and lists
Sites with fewer than twenty pages, where reading them is quicker than auditing
create-a-page-quality-audit.formulaOrCode:
Quality standard (score each: 0 fail, 1 pass)
  1 Owner        A named, current employee is recorded as content owner
  2 Fresh        Reviewed or modified within 12 months (6 for policies, how-to and contact pages)
  3 Accurate     Owner confirms the content is correct and still needed
  4 Title        Title says what the page is about; no "Untitled", "Copy of", "Page 1"
  5 Summary      Description filled in (used by search results and page cards)
  6 Links        No broken links; links have meaningful text that names the destination
  7 Structure    One H1 (the title), headings in order, short paragraphs
  8 Accessible   Images have alt text; no text embedded in images; tables have headers
  9 Findable     Page is in navigation or linked from a parent page; has topic metadata
  10 Used        Viewed in the last 90 days (if not, ask whether it is needed)
  8-10 good   5-7 fix within 30 days   0-4 fix or retire

Add page metadata (Site Pages library > add columns)
  ContentOwner (Person)   ReviewDate (Date)   PageTopic (managed metadata or choice)   AuditScore (Number)
  AuditNotes (Multiple lines)   AuditStatus (Choice: Not audited | Pass | Fix needed | Retire)
  Show them in page details so authors fill them in when publishing.

Inventory (PnP PowerShell)
  Connect-PnPOnline -Url https://contoso.sharepoint.com/sites/intranet -Interactive
  Get-PnPListItem -List "Site Pages" -PageSize 500 |
    Select-Object @{n="Page";e={$_["FileLeafRef"]}}, @{n="Title";e={$_["Title"]}},
                  @{n="Modified";e={$_["Modified"]}}, @{n="Editor";e={$_["Editor"].LookupValue}},
                  @{n="Owner";e={$_["ContentOwner"].LookupValue}}, @{n="Description";e={$_["Description"]}},
                  @{n="Promoted";e={$_["PromotedState"]}} |
    Export-Csv .\pages.csv -NoTypeInformation
  # PromotedState 2 = news post. Audit news separately: old news is expected, wrong reference pages are not.

Usage
  Site contents > Site usage for popular pages; per page: Page details > Analytics.
  For all pages, export from Microsoft 365 usage reports or the audit log (PageViewed events).

Views in the Site Pages library
  Audit: stale        Modified < [Today]-365, PromotedState = 0
  Audit: no owner     ContentOwner is empty
  Audit: no summary   Description is empty
  Audit: fix needed   AuditStatus = Fix needed, group by ContentOwner

Automated checks
  Titles:   filter Title for "Untitled", "Copy", "Test"
  Links:    Site contents has no built-in link checker for modern pages. Run a crawler against the site's
            URLs, or use Page diagnostics. Record broken links in AuditNotes.
  Alt text: open the page in edit mode; the accessibility assistant (Check accessibility in the toolbar) flags
            images without alt text and heading order problems.

Owner request (one message per owner, from a flow grouping pages by ContentOwner)
  Subject: <n> intranet pages need your review by <date>
  For each page: title with link, last modified, views in 90 days, issues found.
  Ask for one of three actions per page: confirm (set ReviewDate), fix, or retire.

Retiring a page
  Unpublish or delete (recycle bin 93 days), remove it from navigation, and redirect inbound links by
  editing the pages that link to it. Search drops it after the next crawl.

Summary after each audit
  Pages audited, average score, pages with no owner, stale pages, retired pages, and change since last audit.

Keep it going
  Review reminder flow: weekly, pages where ReviewDate is older than 12 months, one email per owner.
  Make ContentOwner required for publishing with a page approval flow or column validation.
stepByStepInstructions: Agree the quality checks and scoring.
Add owner, review date and audit columns to the Site Pages library.
Export the page inventory and usage.
Score pages using the views and automated checks.
Send each owner one list of their pages and required actions.
Retire unneeded pages and fix navigation.
Report the results and schedule review reminders.
commonMistakes: Auditing design details while ignoring whether content is correct.
No named owner per page, so nobody acts on findings.
Treating old news posts as stale content.
Running the audit once and never again.
troubleshooting: If ContentOwner is empty for most pages, fill it from the last editor as a starting point and ask owners to correct it.
If the export misses pages, raise the page size and check for folders in the Site Pages library.
If usage data is missing for a page, it had no views in the period or analytics is delayed by a day or two.
If retired pages still show in search, wait for the crawl or request reindexing of the library.

faqs.question: How do I audit SharePoint pages?
faqs.answer: Export the Site Pages library with owner, modified date and usage, score each page against a short checklist, and send owners their pages to confirm, fix or retire.

faqs.question: How do I find old pages on a SharePoint site?
faqs.answer: Create a view of the Site Pages library filtered to pages modified more than a year ago, excluding news posts.

faqs.question: How often should intranet content be reviewed?
faqs.answer: At least yearly for reference pages and every six months for policies, how-to and contact information.

create-a-stale-content-cleanup-process.shortDescription: Find and deal with stale files in a SharePoint library: report what has not been touched, ask owners to keep, archive or delete, and act on the answers safely.
create-a-stale-content-cleanup-process.fullDescription: Inside active sites, libraries fill with files nobody has opened in years. A clean-up process reports files past an age threshold, groups them by owner or folder, asks for a decision, then moves or deletes with the recycle bin as a safety net. Run on a schedule, it keeps libraries useful without anyone deleting on a hunch.
create-a-stale-content-cleanup-process.problemStatement: A library has 40,000 files. Most are from finished work, search results are full of them, and nobody will delete anything without being told it is safe.
whenToUse: Active sites with large libraries
Before a migration, restructure or Copilot rollout
Storage pressure on specific sites
whenNotToUse: Libraries governed by retention labels, where Purview decides what is deleted
Whole sites that are finished, which should go through site archiving instead
create-a-stale-content-cleanup-process.formulaOrCode:
Rules (agree with the site owner first)
  Stale        = not modified for 24 months (pick 12, 24 or 36 by content type)
  Exempt       = files with a retention label, templates, anything in folders named "Reference" or "Records"
  Decisions    = Keep (reset the clock for 12 months) | Archive (move to an archive library) | Delete
  No decision  = after 30 days and two reminders, archive (never delete by default)

Columns to add to the library
  CleanupDecision (Choice: Keep | Archive | Delete)     CleanupDecidedBy (Person)     CleanupDecidedOn (Date)
  CleanupCycle (Text, for example 2026-11)              KeepUntil (Date)

View: "Stale files"
  Modified < [Today]-730    AND   CleanupDecision is empty   AND   (KeepUntil is empty OR KeepUntil < [Today])
  Show: Name, Folder path, Modified, Modified By, File size, CleanupDecision      Index Modified.
  Owners can multi-select in grid view and set CleanupDecision in bulk.

Report (PnP PowerShell) for large libraries
  Connect-PnPOnline -Url https://contoso.sharepoint.com/sites/projects -Interactive
  $cutoff = (Get-Date).AddMonths(-24)
  Get-PnPListItem -List "Documents" -PageSize 2000 -Fields FileLeafRef, FileRef, Modified, Editor, File_x0020_Size, FSObjType |
    Where-Object { $_["FSObjType"] -eq 0 -and $_["Modified"] -lt $cutoff } |
    Select-Object @{n="Name";e={$_["FileLeafRef"]}}, @{n="Path";e={$_["FileRef"]}},
                  @{n="Modified";e={$_["Modified"]}}, @{n="ModifiedBy";e={$_["Editor"].Email}},
                  @{n="SizeMB";e={[math]::Round($_["File_x0020_Size"] / 1MB, 2)}} |
    Export-Csv .\stale-files.csv -NoTypeInformation
  # Summarise by top-level folder and by ModifiedBy to decide who to ask.
  # Version history can hold more storage than the files: Site settings > Storage metrics shows totals per folder.

Flow 1: ask for decisions (Recurrence, first Monday of each quarter)
  Get files (properties only): Filter Query  Modified lt '@{addDays(utcNow(), -730)}'   Top count 5000, pagination on
  Filter array: CleanupDecision empty, no retention label, not in exempt folders
  Select: Name, Link, Modified, Editor email
  Group by editor (or by the folder's owner from a small "Folder Owners" list):
    union(body('Select_editors'), body('Select_editors')) gives the distinct list to loop over
  Send one email per owner with an HTML table (cap at 100 rows and link to the Stale files view for the rest).
  Update each file: CleanupCycle = formatDateTime(utcNow(), 'yyyy-MM')
  Files whose last editor has left go to the site owner.

Flow 2: act on decisions (Recurrence, weekly)
  Keep     > Update file properties: KeepUntil = addToTime(utcNow(), 12, 'Month'); clear CleanupDecision
  Archive  > Move file (SharePoint "Move file" action) to the "Archive" library in the same site, same folder path
             Archive library: read-only for members, excluded from search (Library settings > Advanced > Allow items
             to appear in search results: No)
  Delete   > Delete file (goes to the site recycle bin for 93 days). Log name, path, size, decided by, date
             to a "Cleanup Log" list first.
  Cycle older than 30 days with no decision > treat as Archive

Safety checks in flow 2
  Skip files modified since the decision was recorded (someone started using them again).
  Skip checked-out files and files with a retention label (the delete would fail or be held).
  Process at most a few thousand files per run to stay within connector limits.

After each cycle
  Report files reviewed, kept, archived, deleted, storage released (Storage metrics before and after).
  Empty the archive library on its own schedule, for example delete items archived more than 3 years ago,
  if records policy allows.

Tell people
  Announce the cycle on the site's home page: what counts as stale, the decision deadline, and that archived
  files can be restored on request.
stepByStepInstructions: Agree the stale threshold, exemptions and default action with the site owner.
Add the clean-up columns and the Stale files view.
Run the report to see scale and who to ask.
Send owners their lists and a deadline.
Run the flow that keeps, archives or deletes according to decisions.
Log every deletion and report storage released.
Repeat each quarter or half-year.
commonMistakes: Deleting by age alone without asking anyone.
Making deletion the default when nobody answers.
Ignoring retention labels and checked-out files.
Forgetting that version history, not current files, may be using the space.
troubleshooting: If the view hits the list view threshold, index Modified and filter on it first.
If Move file fails, the destination has a file of the same name or the path is too long. Add a suffix or shorten the folder structure.
If deletes fail, the file is labelled, on hold or checked out. Skip and report it.
If storage does not drop after deletion, files are still in the recycle bins or held by retention.

faqs.question: How do I find old files in a SharePoint library?
faqs.answer: Create a view filtered on Modified earlier than a date offset from today, or export items with PnP PowerShell and filter by modified date.

faqs.question: Is it safe to delete old SharePoint files automatically?
faqs.answer: Only after owners have decided and exemptions are respected. Archive by default, log deletions and rely on the 93-day recycle bin as a safety net.

faqs.question: Why is my SharePoint site still full after deleting files?
faqs.answer: Deleted files count until they leave both recycle bins, and version history or retention holds may be keeping copies.

create-a-metadata-standards-guide.shortDescription: A metadata standard for SharePoint: which columns every library carries, how they are named and typed, where the values come from, and who may change them.
create-a-metadata-standards-guide.fullDescription: Metadata only pays off when it is consistent. A short standard defines a core set of site columns, naming rules, when to use choice, managed metadata or lookup, and how terms are requested and changed. Applied through content types, it makes search, views, retention and automation work the same way on every site.
create-a-metadata-standards-guide.problemStatement: One site has a Department column, another has Dept, a third uses folders. Values include 'HR', 'H.R.' and 'Human Resources', so nothing can be filtered or rolled up across sites.
whenToUse: Tenants with many sites built by different people
Before a migration, intranet build or search improvement project
When flows and reports depend on column values
whenNotToUse: A single team site with one library, where a few local columns are enough
Short-lived project sites that will be archived as a whole
create-a-metadata-standards-guide.formulaOrCode:
1. Core columns (site columns published from the content type hub; every document content type includes them)
  Display name      Internal name     Type                Values from              Required
  Document Type     DocumentType      Managed metadata    term set "Document Types"   yes
  Department        Department        Managed metadata    term set "Departments"      yes
  Document Owner    DocumentOwner     Person              directory                   yes
  Status            DocStatus         Choice              Draft | Final | Superseded  yes, default Draft
  Review Date       ReviewDate        Date                                           where reviewed
  Sensitivity       (sensitivity label, applied by Purview, not a custom column)
  Optional by content type: Project, Customer, Contract Number, Effective Date

2. Naming rules
  Internal name: create the column with no spaces in PascalCase (DocumentOwner), then rename the display name.
    The internal name never changes afterwards and is what flows, formulas and search use.
  Avoid names SharePoint reserves or already uses: Title, Name, Author, Editor, Created, Modified, ID, Status.
  Display names in sentence case, singular: "Document owner", not "Document_Owners".
  One column for one meaning across the tenant. Reuse the site column; do not recreate it per list.
  Prefix nothing. Group site columns under a group named for the organisation: "Contoso Columns".

3. Choosing the column type
  Choice             fewer than about 15 values, stable, used in one or two lists
  Managed metadata   shared across sites, hierarchical, needs synonyms, or changes centrally
  Lookup             values are records with their own columns in the same site (customers, projects)
  Person             anything that names a user; never free text
  Yes/No             true binary facts only; a three-state answer is a choice
  Date               dates; never text such as "Q3"
  Single line text   identifiers and free text; add validation for patterns
  Avoid: multi-value columns where a single value will do (they cannot be sorted or grouped and limit filters),
         calculated columns for anything a flow or app must write, and more than 12 lookup, person and
         managed metadata columns in one view (lookup threshold).

4. Term sets (Term store admin centre)
  Global term sets: Departments, Document Types, Locations. Owned by a named term set owner.
  Closed submission policy: only owners add terms. Users request terms through a request list.
  Each term: a default label, synonyms for common variants (HR, Human Resources), a description.
  Never delete a term that is in use. Deprecate it so existing items keep the value and new items cannot pick it.

5. Content types
  Create in the content type hub (SharePoint admin centre > Content services > Content type gallery).
  Base "Contoso Document" carries the core columns. Specific types inherit from it:
    Contoso Document > Policy, Contract, Project Document, Meeting Record
  Publish to the hubs or sites that need them. Add to libraries and set the default content type.
  Site-specific columns are allowed on top; changing core columns locally is not.

6. Defaults that save typing
  Library settings > Column default value settings: set Department or Project per library or per folder,
  so files inherit values when uploaded to that location.
  Document sets for groups of files that share values.

7. Search
  Managed properties: map crawled properties of core columns to refinable properties
    ows_taxId_DocumentType > RefinableString00 (alias DocumentType)
    ows_ReviewDate         > RefinableDate00   (alias ReviewDate)
  Reindex the library after mapping. Use them in search verticals, filters and the PnP search web parts.

8. Change control
  Request: who asks, what column or term, why, which sites.
  Decide: metadata owner within 5 working days. Record decisions in a "Metadata Decisions" list.
  Changes to core columns go through the content type hub and are republished; never edited in a site.
  Review the standard yearly, and term sets every six months for unused and duplicate terms.

9. Checks
  View per library: items where a required core column is empty.
  Quarterly report of columns created locally with names close to core columns (Dept, Doc Type) for consolidation.
stepByStepInstructions: Agree the core columns and who owns the standard.
Write the naming rules and column type guidance.
Create the global term sets with owners and synonyms.
Build the base content type and its children in the content type hub and publish them.
Set library and folder default values.
Map the core columns to managed properties for search.
Set up the change request route and periodic checks.
commonMistakes: Creating columns with spaces, producing internal names such as Document_x0020_Owner.
Recreating the same column list by list.
Free-text columns for departments and people.
Deleting terms that existing items still use.
troubleshooting: If a published content type does not appear in a site, publishing can take time. Check the content type's publishing status and the site's content type log.
If a managed metadata column shows a GUID or is blank in a flow, read the Label property of the column value.
If search refiners show nothing, the managed property mapping is missing or the library has not been reindexed.
If a view fails with a lookup threshold message, reduce the lookup, person and managed metadata columns shown to twelve or fewer.

faqs.question: What metadata should every SharePoint document have?
faqs.answer: A small core set such as document type, department, owner and status, delivered through a shared content type so every library uses the same columns.

faqs.question: Should I use choice columns or managed metadata?
faqs.answer: Use choice for short, stable lists used in one place. Use managed metadata when values are shared across sites, hierarchical or centrally maintained.

faqs.question: How do I keep column names consistent across sites?
faqs.answer: Define site columns once in the content type hub, publish them through content types and require changes to go through a named metadata owner.

create-a-document-routing-automation.shortDescription: A Power Automate flow that routes uploaded documents by their metadata: moves each file to the right library or folder, assigns a reviewer and records where it went.
create-a-document-routing-automation.fullDescription: A single drop-off library is easy for users, but someone then has to sort the files. A routing flow reads each new file's type and department, looks up the destination and reviewer in a rules list, moves the file, sets its properties and logs the result. Rules live in data, so adding a route does not mean editing the flow.
create-a-document-routing-automation.problemStatement: People upload everything to one library. Files wait for someone to drag them to the right place, and some never get there.
whenToUse: Intake libraries for invoices, contracts, forms or scanned mail
When destination depends on document type, department or value
When routing rules change often
whenNotToUse: Users can save directly to the right place with default metadata by folder
Classification needs to read document content, which calls for AI Builder or Syntex models ahead of this flow
create-a-document-routing-automation.formulaOrCode:
Lists
  Routing Rules:  Title | DocumentType (text) | Department (text, optional) | DestinationSite (URL) |
                  DestinationLibrary (server-relative path, for example /sites/finance/Invoices) |
                  DestinationFolder (text, optional, supports {yyyy} and {MM}) | ReviewerEmail | IsActive | Priority (number)
  Routing Log:    Title (file name) | SourcePath | DestinationPath | RuleUsed | Result | Message | RoutedOn

Intake library "Inbox"
  Required columns: DocumentType (choice), Department (choice). RoutingStatus (choice: Waiting | Routed | Needs attention)

Trigger: SharePoint - When a file is created or modified (properties only), library Inbox
  Trigger condition (run only when metadata is complete and the file is not yet routed):
    @and(not(empty(triggerOutputs()?['body/DocumentType/Value'])),
         not(equals(triggerOutputs()?['body/RoutingStatus/Value'], 'Routed')),
         not(equals(triggerOutputs()?['body/RoutingStatus/Value'], 'Needs attention')))
  Settings > Concurrency control: On, degree 1 if file names can clash; otherwise 5

Scope: Try
  1. Get file properties (ID from trigger)            fresh values and check-out state
  2. Condition: file is checked out?
       not(empty(outputs('Get_file_properties')?['body/CheckoutUser']))   > Terminate (Cancelled). The next
       modification (check-in) triggers the flow again.
  3. Get items (Routing Rules)
       Filter Query:  DocumentType eq '@{outputs('Get_file_properties')?['body/DocumentType/Value']}' and IsActive eq 1
       Order By:      Priority asc
  4. Filter array (department match or rule has no department):
       @or(empty(item()?['Department']),
           equals(item()?['Department'], outputs('Get_file_properties')?['body/Department/Value']))
  5. Compose Rule:     first(body('Filter_array'))
  6. Condition: empty(outputs('Rule'))  > yes: Update file properties RoutingStatus = Needs attention; notify the
       intake owner; Terminate (Succeeded)
  7. Compose Folder:
       replace(replace(coalesce(outputs('Rule')?['DestinationFolder'], ''),
               '{yyyy}', formatDateTime(utcNow(), 'yyyy')), '{MM}', formatDateTime(utcNow(), 'MM'))
  8. Send an HTTP request to SharePoint (destination site): make sure the folder exists
       POST _api/web/folders/AddUsingPath(decodedurl='@{outputs('Rule')?['DestinationLibrary']}/@{outputs('Folder')}')
       (returns the folder whether or not it existed; skip when Folder is empty)
  9. Move file (SharePoint)
       Current Site: intake site     File to Move: Identifier from Get file properties
       Destination Site: Rule DestinationSite     Destination Folder: DestinationLibrary/Folder
       If another file is already there: Move with a new name
  10. Update file properties at the destination (site and library from the rule; ID from Move file output)
       Reviewer Claims: i:0#.f|membership|<ReviewerEmail>      ReviewStatus: Waiting for review
       DocumentType, Department carried across if the destination has those columns
       (Move keeps metadata only for columns that exist in both libraries with the same internal name.)
  11. Send an email or Teams message to the reviewer with a link to the moved file
  12. Create item (Routing Log): Result = Routed, DestinationPath, RuleUsed

Scope: Catch   (Configure run after: Try has failed or timed out)
  1. Filter array on result('Try') where status eq 'Failed'; Compose first message:
       first(body('Filter_failed'))?['error']?['message']
  2. Update file properties (Inbox): RoutingStatus = Needs attention   (if the file is still there)
  3. Create item (Routing Log): Result = Failed, Message
  4. Notify the intake owner. Terminate (Failed) so the run shows as failed.

Dynamic destination note
  Update file properties needs a fixed library to show its columns at design time. For destinations that vary,
  use Send an HTTP request to SharePoint with ValidateUpdateListItem:
    POST _api/web/GetFileByServerRelativePath(decodedurl='<path>')/ListItemAllFields/ValidateUpdateListItem
    Body: { "formValues": [ { "FieldName": "ReviewStatus", "FieldValue": "Waiting for review" } ] }

Files that sit in the Inbox
  Scheduled flow, daily: files in Inbox older than 2 days with RoutingStatus Waiting or Needs attention,
  one digest to the intake owner.
stepByStepInstructions: Create the routing rules and routing log lists.
Add required type and department columns and a routing status to the intake library.
Add the trigger with a condition so only complete, unrouted files start the flow.
Look up the matching rule and handle the no-rule case.
Create the destination folder if needed and move the file.
Set reviewer and status at the destination and notify the reviewer.
Log the result and handle failures in a catch scope.
commonMistakes: Hard-coding destinations in a Switch that grows with every new route.
Moving files that are still checked out or missing metadata.
Expecting metadata to survive a move when the destination lacks the same columns.
No log, so a missing file cannot be traced.
troubleshooting: If the flow fires several times per upload, add the trigger condition and set RoutingStatus as the first update.
If Move file fails with a locked file message, the document is open or checked out. Retry later or wait for check-in.
If metadata is blank after the move, create the same site columns in the destination library.
If no rule matches because of spacing or case, standardise DocumentType values with choice columns on both sides.

faqs.question: How do I move files to different SharePoint libraries automatically?
faqs.answer: Trigger a flow when a file is created or modified, read its metadata, look up the destination in a rules list and use the Move file action.
