whenNotToUse: Organisation-wide configuration, which belongs in a settings list or environment variables that only admins change
Storing anything sensitive in user-editable settings
create-a-reusable-app-settings-panel.formulaOrCode:
Storage: list "User Settings"
  Title (user email, lower case, indexed), AppName (text), SettingsJson (multi-line plain text), Modified
  One row per user per app. JSON keeps the list stable when you add a preference.

Defaults (App.Formulas)
  nfDefaultSettings = { DefaultTab: "Mine", PageSize: 15, Density: "Comfortable", Theme: "Light", EmailDigest: true };
  nfAppName = "RequestHub";
  nfUserEmail = Lower(User().Email);

Load at start (App.OnStart)
  Set(gblSettingsRow, LookUp('User Settings', Title = nfUserEmail && AppName = nfAppName));
  Set(gblSettings,
      If(IsBlank(gblSettingsRow) || IsBlank(gblSettingsRow.SettingsJson),
         nfDefaultSettings,
         With({ j: ParseJSON(gblSettingsRow.SettingsJson) },
              { DefaultTab:  Coalesce(Text(j.DefaultTab), nfDefaultSettings.DefaultTab),
                PageSize:    Coalesce(Value(j.PageSize), nfDefaultSettings.PageSize),
                Density:     Coalesce(Text(j.Density), nfDefaultSettings.Density),
                Theme:       Coalesce(Text(j.Theme), nfDefaultSettings.Theme),
                EmailDigest: Coalesce(Boolean(j.EmailDigest), nfDefaultSettings.EmailDigest) })))
  Coalesce supplies the default for any preference added after the user last saved.

Use the settings
  Home tab at start:      Set(locTab, gblSettings.DefaultTab)
  Gallery page size:      gblSettings.PageSize
  Row height:             If(gblSettings.Density = "Compact", 40, 64)
  Colours:                If(gblSettings.Theme = "Dark", ColorValue("#1F1F1F"), Color.White)

Component: cmpSettingsPanel (component library, so every app gets updates)
  Custom properties
    Settings        Input, Record       the current settings
    IsOpen          Input, Boolean
    OnSave          Event (behaviour), with a parameter NewSettings (Record)
    OnClose         Event (behaviour)
  Layout: full-height panel 360 wide on the right, with a dimmed rectangle behind it.
    Visible: cmpSettingsPanel.IsOpen
  Controls
    drpTab      Items: ["Mine", "New", "All open"]          Default: cmpSettingsPanel.Settings.DefaultTab
    drpPageSize Items: [10, 15, 25, 50]                     Default: cmpSettingsPanel.Settings.PageSize
    radDensity  Items: ["Comfortable", "Compact"]           Default: cmpSettingsPanel.Settings.Density
    radTheme    Items: ["Light", "Dark"]                    Default: cmpSettingsPanel.Settings.Theme
    tglDigest   Default: cmpSettingsPanel.Settings.EmailDigest
    btnSave.OnSelect:
      cmpSettingsPanel.OnSave({ DefaultTab: drpTab.Selected.Value, PageSize: drpPageSize.Selected.Value,
                                Density: radDensity.Selected.Value, Theme: radTheme.Selected.Value,
                                EmailDigest: tglDigest.Value })
    btnCancel.OnSelect / backdrop OnSelect: cmpSettingsPanel.OnClose()
    btnReset.OnSelect: cmpSettingsPanel.OnSave(nfDefaultSettings)       (pass defaults in as another input for reuse)

In the app
  Gear icon OnSelect: Set(gblShowSettings, true)
  cmpSettingsPanel_1.Settings: gblSettings        IsOpen: gblShowSettings
  OnClose: Set(gblShowSettings, false)
  OnSave:
    Set(gblSettings, NewSettings);
    IfError(
        Set(gblSettingsRow,
            Patch('User Settings', Coalesce(gblSettingsRow, Defaults('User Settings')),
                  { Title: nfUserEmail, AppName: nfAppName, SettingsJson: JSON(NewSettings, JSONFormat.Compact) })),
        Notify("Preferences applied for this session but not saved: " & FirstError.Message, NotificationType.Warning),
        Notify("Preferences saved", NotificationType.Success));
    Set(gblShowSettings, false)
  Applying to gblSettings first means the app responds immediately even if the save is slow.

Permissions on the list
  Advanced settings > Item-level permissions: read and edit only items created by the user.
  Users need Contribute on the list. Admin-only settings never go in this list.

Accessibility
  Panel title as a heading, focus moves to the first control when opened (SetFocus(drpTab)), Escape or Cancel
  closes, and every control has an AccessibleLabel.
stepByStepInstructions: Create a User Settings list with one row per user and app holding a JSON string.
Define default settings as a named formula.
Load the user's row at start and merge it with the defaults.
Build the panel as a component with a settings input and save and close events.
On save, apply the new settings to a global variable and patch the user's row.
Restrict list items to their creator and read settings throughout the app.
commonMistakes: A column per preference, forcing a list change for each new option.
No defaults for users with no saved row.
Mixing admin configuration with user preferences.
Waiting for the save before applying the change on screen.
troubleshooting: If preferences are not remembered, check the lookup uses the lower-case email and the right app name.
If a new preference is blank for existing users, add a Coalesce default when parsing.
If two rows exist for one user, patch the stored row variable instead of always creating.
If the component's defaults do not refresh, reset the controls when the panel opens.

faqs.question: How do I save user preferences in Power Apps?
faqs.answer: Store them as JSON in a per-user row of a settings list, load the row at start and merge it with defaults.

faqs.question: Why store settings as JSON?
faqs.answer: New preferences can be added without changing the list, and older rows fall back to defaults for missing values.

faqs.question: How do I reuse a settings panel across apps?
faqs.answer: Build it as a component in a component library with a settings input and a save event.

create-a-maker-handoff-checklist.shortDescription: A checklist to run on the day a canvas app changes hands: ownership, connections, flows, data access and a walkthrough, each with a way to prove it is done.
create-a-maker-handoff-checklist.fullDescription: A handoff package describes the app. The checklist is what you tick through at the handover meeting to prove the new maker can open, edit, publish and support it without the previous maker. Most failed handoffs come down to one missed item: a flow still running on the leaver's connection, or a list the new owner cannot edit.
create-a-maker-handoff-checklist.problemStatement: A maker moves teams and shares the app as co-owner on their last day. A month later the flows stop because their account is disabled, and the new owner finds they cannot edit the SharePoint list or see the flow run history.
whenToUse: A maker leaving, changing role or handing an app to a support team
Moving an app from a pilot maker to IT ownership
Before removing a departing user's licence or account
whenNotToUse: Documenting how the app works, which belongs in the handoff package
Apps being retired, which need a decommission list instead
create-a-maker-handoff-checklist.formulaOrCode:
MAKER HANDOFF CHECKLIST            App: ____________   From: ________   To: ________   Date: ________

1. Ownership and access                                              Proof
[ ] New maker is co-owner of the app (or owner, set by an admin)     Opens the app in edit mode
[ ] New maker is co-owner of every flow the app calls                Sees run history for each flow
[ ] New maker has edit rights on each list, library or table        Edits a test row directly
[ ] New maker has the Environment Maker role (and a security role    Saves and publishes a trivial change
    covering the tables, for Dataverse)
[ ] A second owner exists for the app and each flow                  Two names shown under Owners
[ ] Security groups used for sharing have an owner who is staying    Group owner checked in Entra

2. Connections and identities
[ ] Every flow connection is listed with whose account it uses       Table below completed
[ ] Connections on the leaver's account are replaced                 Flow runs succeed after the change
[ ] Service account password or secret holder is identified          Named person or vault entry
[ ] Connection references (solution flows) point to the new or       Checked in the solution
    service connection
[ ] Shared mailboxes, Teams and channels the flows post to:          New maker can send a test
    new maker is a member

    Flow / connector         Account used today        Replace with        Done
    ______________________   _______________________   _________________   [ ]

3. The app itself
[ ] Latest published version matches the latest saved version        Versions tab checked
[ ] App is in a solution, or the export (.msapp) is stored in the    File location recorded
    team library
[ ] App checker shows no errors                                      Screenshot or note
[ ] Known issues and workarounds are written down                    Link to the package
[ ] Hard-coded emails, IDs and URLs are listed                       Search for "@" and "https://" done

4. Data and security
[ ] Who can use the app, and through which group                     Share panel reviewed
[ ] Row-level or role rules are explained (role lists, security      New maker changes a test role
    lists, item permissions)
[ ] Personal or sensitive data in the app is noted                   Entry in the data register
[ ] Backups or recycle bin recovery steps are known                  Restore of a test item tried

5. Operations
[ ] Support contact shown to users is updated                        About screen or help link checked
[ ] Failure alerts for flows go to the new owner or a team mailbox   Test failure alert received
[ ] Scheduled jobs and their timings are listed                      Recurrence flows reviewed
[ ] Licence needs (premium connectors, per-app plans) are known      Licence check done

6. Walkthrough (60 minutes, new maker drives)
[ ] Submit a record as a user                [ ] Approve or process it as each role
[ ] Change a formula, save, publish, and restore the previous version
[ ] Turn a flow off and on, resubmit a failed run
[ ] Add a choice value or setting used by the app

7. Sign-off
Outgoing maker ____________   Incoming maker ____________   Business owner ____________
Follow-up check booked for 30 days after handoff: ____________

After the leaver's account is disabled, re-test every flow. A connection that worked the day before can
fail once the account is blocked.
stepByStepInstructions: Schedule the handover meeting before the outgoing maker's last week.
Add the new maker and a second owner to the app, flows and data sources.
List every connection and replace those on the leaver's account.
Confirm versions, storage of the source and known issues.
Have the new maker drive the walkthrough tasks.
Sign off and book a check for 30 days later.
commonMistakes: Sharing the app but not the flows or the data.
Leaving flows on the leaver's connections.
Ticking items without proof.
Running the handoff on the maker's last day with no time to fix gaps.
troubleshooting: If flows fail after the account is disabled, edit each flow and switch its connections to the new owner or a service account.
If the new maker cannot see a flow, add them as co-owner from the flow's details page or have an admin do it.
If the app cannot be edited, check the Environment Maker role as well as co-ownership.
If the original owner has already left, an admin can set a new owner with the Power Apps admin PowerShell cmdlets.

faqs.question: What should a Power Apps handoff checklist include?
faqs.answer: Ownership of the app and flows, data permissions, connections, source storage, support contacts and a hands-on walkthrough by the new maker.

faqs.question: What breaks when a maker leaves?
faqs.answer: Flows running on the maker's connections stop when the account is disabled, and nobody else can edit an app with a single owner.

faqs.question: Can an admin change the owner of a canvas app?
faqs.answer: Yes. A Power Platform admin can assign a new owner with the admin PowerShell cmdlets or from the admin centre.

create-a-delegation-review-worksheet.shortDescription: A worksheet for auditing every data call in a canvas app for delegation: the formula, the source, whether it delegates, how many rows it could miss and the fix.
create-a-delegation-review-worksheet.fullDescription: Delegation problems hide until a list grows past the row limit, then users report missing records. Reviewing an app formula by formula with a worksheet finds them first. Each row records where the query is, what it does, whether the data source can run it, the realistic row count and the chosen remedy.
create-a-delegation-review-worksheet.problemStatement: An app worked in testing with 200 rows. In production the list has 6,000, the gallery shows only some matches and totals are wrong, and nobody knows which of the 40 formulas are affected.
whenToUse: Before go-live of any app on a source that will exceed 500 rows
When users report missing records or wrong counts
As part of a formula or performance review
whenNotToUse: Apps whose sources will always stay under a few hundred rows
Collections loaded deliberately in full, where the load itself is the only query to check
create-a-delegation-review-worksheet.formulaOrCode:
DELEGATION REVIEW WORKSHEET        App: ____________   Reviewer: ________   Date: ________
Data row limit setting: ____ (Settings > General; default 500, maximum 2,000)

Find the queries
  1. App checker > Formulas: note every delegation warning (yellow triangle, blue underline).
  2. Search the app (Ctrl+F in the Search pane) for: Filter(  LookUp(  Search(  Sort  CountRows(  Sum(
     CountIf(  First(  Last(  in   ForAll(   AddColumns(   Distinct(   GroupBy(
  3. Check OnStart, OnVisible, gallery Items, combo box Items and every button that reads data.
  Warnings do not appear for every case (for example CountRows on some sources, or queries inside
  collections), so the search matters as much as the checker.

Record each one
  # | Screen.Control.Property      | Formula (shortened)                          | Source     | Rows now / in 2 yrs | Delegates? | Risk | Fix
  1 | scrHome.galQueue.Items       | Filter(Requests, Status.Value = "Open")      | SharePoint | 6,000 / 15,000      | Yes        | Low  | none
  2 | scrHome.galQueue.Items       | ... && txtSearch.Text in Title               | SharePoint | 6,000               | No         | High | StartsWith
  3 | scrHome.lblCount.Text        | CountRows(Filter(Requests, ...))             | SharePoint | 6,000               | No         | High | count in a flow or collection
  4 | scrEdit.cmbOwner.Items       | Filter(Staff, Active)                        | SharePoint | 300                 | Yes        | Low  | none
  5 | App.OnStart                  | ClearCollect(colAll, Requests)               | SharePoint | 6,000               | Capped     | High | filter first
  6 | scrReport.galByTeam.Items    | GroupBy(Requests, Team, Rows)                | SharePoint | 6,000               | No         | High | pre-filter to period

Quick reference: SharePoint
  Delegates:      =, <>, <, >, <=, >= on text, number and date columns; StartsWith on text;
                  And, Or, Not; Sort and SortByColumns on simple columns; Filter on choice (.Value),
                  lookup (.Value or .Id), person (.Email) and yes/no columns with =
  Does not:       in, exactin, Search, EndsWith, Len, Trim, Left, Lower, IsBlank on some column types,
                  date functions applied to the column (Year(Created)), CountRows, Sum, Average, Distinct,
                  GroupBy, Last, comparisons with complex or calculated columns
Quick reference: Dataverse
  Delegates far more: Search, in for choices, Sum, Min, Max, Average, CountRows and CountIf up to 50,000 rows,
  views as pre-built filters. Still not: Len, Trim, most text manipulation on the column side.

Rate the risk
  High:   not delegable and the source can exceed the row limit before the non-delegable part runs
  Medium: not delegable, but a delegable filter always reduces rows below the limit first
  Low:    fully delegable, or the source cannot grow

Fix catalogue
  Search with in            ->  StartsWith(Title, txtSearch.Text), or a keyword column with StartsWith
  Date function on column   ->  compare to a range: Created >= dtStart && Created < dtEnd
  Lower(Email) = ...        ->  store emails lower-case and compare directly
  Counts and sums           ->  a flow, a calculated total on a parent row, or a collection of a delegable subset
  Non-delegable test        ->  With({ base: Filter(Source, delegable conditions) }, Filter(base, other tests))
                               valid only when base is always under the row limit
  Whole-list ClearCollect   ->  filter to what the user needs (mine, open, this year)
  Last(...)                 ->  First(Sort(Source, ID, SortOrder.Descending))
  More than 2,000 needed    ->  paging by ID ranges, or move the data to Dataverse

Test
  Set the data row limit to 1 temporarily (Settings > General) and run the app. Any gallery, count or lookup
  that now shows wrong results depends on local processing. Set the limit back afterwards.

Sign-off
  High-risk rows remaining: ____    Accepted by owner: ________    Re-review when the source passes ____ rows
stepByStepInstructions: Record the app's data row limit and list every data source with current and expected row counts.
Collect delegation warnings from the app checker.
Search the app for data functions and add each query to the worksheet.
Mark whether each delegates on its source and rate the risk.
Choose a fix from the catalogue for every high-risk row and apply it.
Test with the row limit set to 1, then restore the setting and sign off.
commonMistakes: Raising the row limit to 2,000 and calling it fixed.
Relying only on the yellow warnings.
Testing with a small list.
Forgetting OnStart collections, which are capped silently.
troubleshooting: If a warning remains after a rewrite, check which side of the comparison uses a function and move it to the value side.
If a choice column filter warns, compare the Value property with equals, not in.
If results are still short, check whether an earlier collection was capped at the row limit.
If the test with a limit of 1 breaks everything, fix the highest row-count sources first.

faqs.question: How do I check a Power App for delegation problems?
faqs.answer: List every Filter, LookUp, Search, Sort and aggregate in the app, check whether the source can run each one, and test with the data row limit set to 1.

faqs.question: Does raising the data row limit fix delegation?
faqs.answer: No. It raises the cap to at most 2,000 rows and slows the app. Larger sources still return incomplete results.

faqs.question: Which functions do not delegate to SharePoint?
faqs.answer: Among others: in, Search, EndsWith, Len, Lower, date functions applied to a column, CountRows, Sum, Distinct and GroupBy.

create-a-maker-onboarding-path.shortDescription: A four-week path that takes a new Power Apps maker from first sign-in to a reviewed, shared app: environment, standards, a guided build, review and release.
create-a-maker-onboarding-path.fullDescription: New makers usually start in the default environment with a template and no guidance, then learn the rules when something breaks. An onboarding path gives each new maker an environment, the standards that matter, a small build with checkpoints and a named mentor, so the first app they share is one the organisation can support.
create-a-maker-onboarding-path.problemStatement: Twenty people start making apps this year. Each learns alone, apps appear in the default environment with personal connections and no second owner, and the admin team meets them for the first time when a flow fails.
whenToUse: Organisations with a steady flow of new citizen developers
Champions programmes and centres of excellence
Teams adopting Power Apps for the first time
whenNotToUse: Professional developers joining an established team, who need the ALM guide instead
One-off makers building a personal productivity app that will never be shared
create-a-maker-onboarding-path.formulaOrCode:
MAKER ONBOARDING PATH (4 weeks, about 3 hours a week)

Before day 1 (admin or champion)
  [ ] Developer environment created for the maker (or the maker creates one: Developer plan)
  [ ] Added to the Makers team or community channel
  [ ] Mentor assigned: ____________
  [ ] Welcome message sent with links to this path, the standards and the support channel

Week 1: Set-up and ground rules
  Do
    [ ] Sign in to make.powerapps.com and switch to your developer environment
    [ ] Read the one-page rules: where to build, which connectors are allowed (DLP), what needs approval
    [ ] Complete "Create a canvas app" on Microsoft Learn (about 1 hour)
    [ ] Build a throwaway app from a SharePoint list to see the parts: screens, gallery, form
  Know by the end
    Default environment is for personal productivity only. Shared apps live in a team or project environment.
    Premium connectors and Dataverse need a licence check first.
    Every shared app needs two owners.
  Checkpoint with mentor (20 min): show the throwaway app, ask questions.

Week 2: Build the first real app, the supported way
  Do
    [ ] Pick a small real problem: one list, one or two roles, under five screens
    [ ] Design the list first: columns, types, required fields, an owner
    [ ] Create a solution with the team publisher and build the app inside it
    [ ] Apply the naming standard: scr, gal, btn, txt prefixes; gbl and loc variables; col collections
    [ ] Use named formulas for constants and the current user
  Know by the end
    Delegation: what the blue underline means and why row limits matter.
    Patch with IfError, and Notify for success and failure.
  Checkpoint (30 min): mentor reviews the list design and the first screen.

Week 3: Make it robust
  Do
    [ ] Add validation, empty states and a loading indicator
    [ ] Add one flow in the same solution, using a connection reference
    [ ] Run App checker (formulas, accessibility, performance) and clear the errors
    [ ] Test as a normal user with a second account or a colleague
    [ ] Write the half-page support note: purpose, owner, data, flows, known limits
  Know by the end
    How sharing works: the app, the data and the flow are shared separately.
    How to restore a previous version.
  Checkpoint (30 min): formula review against the checklist.

Week 4: Review and release
  Do
    [ ] Request a release review (form or channel post)
    [ ] Fix review findings
    [ ] Export the solution as managed and import to the team environment, or ask the release owner to
    [ ] Share with a security group, add a second owner, update the app inventory
    [ ] Post a short demo in the makers channel
  Graduation criteria
    [ ] App in a solution, in the right environment, with two owners
    [ ] No delegation warnings on sources that can exceed the row limit
    [ ] No App checker errors; accessibility labels on inputs
    [ ] Support note stored with the app
    [ ] Maker can explain DLP, delegation and sharing in their own words

After graduation
  Month 2: join a formula review as a reviewer.    Month 3: mentor the next new maker.
  Further learning: components, Dataverse basics, pipelines, Power Automate error handling.

Tracking (list "Maker Onboarding")
  Title (maker), Mentor, StartDate, Week (1 to 4), Checkpoint1..4 (dates), AppName, Graduated (yes/no), Notes
  A weekly view of makers with no checkpoint in 14 days shows who is stuck.

Automate the first step
  A flow on the Power Platform for Admins connector can detect a maker's first app and send the welcome
  message with this path.
stepByStepInstructions: Prepare an environment, a mentor and a welcome message for each new maker.
Week 1: cover the rules and a throwaway first app.
Week 2: build a small real app inside a solution using the standards.
Week 3: add validation, a flow, checks and a support note.
Week 4: run a release review and share the app with two owners.
Track progress in a list and bring graduates back as reviewers and mentors.
commonMistakes: Pointing new makers at documentation with no build task.
Letting the first shared app live in the default environment.
No mentor or checkpoints.
Teaching features before the rules on environments, connectors and sharing.
troubleshooting: If makers stall in week 2, shrink the project to one list and three screens.
If makers cannot create a developer environment, check the tenant setting that allows developer environment creation.
If reviews pile up, train graduates as reviewers.
If apps still appear in the default environment, add a welcome flow that reaches makers on their first app.

faqs.question: How should new Power Apps makers be onboarded?
faqs.answer: Give each a developer environment, a mentor and a short path: rules first, then a small real app built in a solution, a review and a supported release.

faqs.question: Where should new makers build apps?
faqs.answer: In a personal developer environment for learning and a team or project environment for shared apps, not the default environment.

faqs.question: How long does maker onboarding take?
faqs.answer: About four weeks at a few hours a week to reach a reviewed, shared first app.

create-a-governed-reference-list.shortDescription: A SharePoint reference list (departments, cost centres, categories) that other lists and apps depend on, set up with stable keys, an active flag, owners and a change process.
create-a-governed-reference-list.fullDescription: Reference lists look trivial until someone renames a department and three apps and two reports break. A governed reference list has a code that never changes, a display name that can, an active flag in place of deletion, restricted edit rights and a short log of changes. Consumers filter on Active and store the code or ID, not the label.
create-a-governed-reference-list.problemStatement: The Departments list is edited by anyone. A row is deleted, lookups go blank in 400 requests, and a flow that switches on the department name stops routing.
whenToUse: Lists used as lookups or drop-down sources by several lists, apps or flows
Values that change a few times a year and need an owner
Codes shared with finance, HR or other systems
whenNotToUse: Three or four fixed values used by one list, where a choice column is simpler
Large hierarchical vocabularies shared across sites, which fit the term store
create-a-governed-reference-list.formulaOrCode:
List: Departments (reference)
  Column          Type                 Settings
  Title           Single line          Display name. Required. Enforce unique values. Indexed.
  Code            Single line          Stable key, e.g. FIN, HR, OPS. Required. Enforce unique values. Indexed.
                                       Column validation: =AND(LEN([Code])>=2,LEN([Code])<=10,EXACT([Code],UPPER([Code])))
  Active          Yes/No               Default Yes. Indexed.
  SortOrder       Number               0 decimals. Default 100.
  OwnerContact    Person               Who to ask about this value.
  ApproverGroup   Single line          Optional data that flows read, e.g. an approver mailbox.
  ValidFrom       Date                 Optional.
  ValidTo         Date                 Optional. List validation: =OR(ISBLANK([ValidTo]),[ValidTo]>=[ValidFrom])
  ReplacedBy      Lookup (this list)   For merged or renamed values.
  Notes           Multiple lines       Plain text.

List settings
  Versioning: on, keep 50 versions.         Attachments: off.         Quick edit: off (Advanced settings).
  Permissions: break inheritance. Members: Read. "Reference Data Stewards" group: Edit. Owners: Full control.
  Deletion: stewards have a custom level without Delete Items, so values are retired, not deleted.

Views
  Active values     Filter: Active = Yes       Sort: SortOrder, Title      (default)
  Retired           Filter: Active = No
  All with history  All items, with Modified and Modified By

Rules for change
  Add      Steward adds the row. Code agreed with finance if it mirrors a system code.
  Rename   Change Title only. Code stays. Lookups show the new name automatically.
  Retire   Set Active = No and ValidTo. Never delete: existing items keep their lookup value.
  Merge    Retire the old row, set ReplacedBy. A flow or script repoints open items if needed.
  Each change is requested through the "Reference Data Changes" list:
    Title, ListName, ChangeType (Add, Rename, Retire, Merge), Value, Reason, RequestedBy, Status, DoneOn

Consuming the list
  SharePoint lookup column       Departments > Title, with Code as an additional field.
                                 Lookup columns cannot filter on Active. Use the app or a form rule to do that.
  Power Apps drop-down           Items: SortByColumns(Filter(Departments, Active), "SortOrder")
                                 Existing records with a retired value still need to show it:
                                 Items: Filter(Departments, Active || ID = ThisItem.Department.Id)
                                 Patch: { Department: { Id: drpDept.Selected.ID, Value: drpDept.Selected.Title } }
  Power Automate                 Get items, Filter Query: Code eq 'FIN'   then read ApproverGroup.
                                 Branch on Code, never on Title.
  Reports                        Join on ID or Code.

Dependency register (in the list description or a Notes page)
  Used by: Requests list (lookup), Request Hub app (drop-down), Approval routing flow (Code), Finance report.
  Check this before any Retire or Merge.

Health check (quarterly)
  Rows with Active = Yes and ValidTo in the past.      Rows with no OwnerContact.
  Codes that differ from the finance system.           Open items pointing at retired values.

Provisioning
  Keep the list in a PnP site template so test and production match, and load rows from a CSV so the IDs
  are created in the same order in each site.
stepByStepInstructions: Create the list with a unique title, a unique stable code, an active flag and a sort order.
Turn on versioning, turn off attachments and quick edit, and restrict edit rights to stewards.
Add views for active and retired values.
Agree the rules for add, rename, retire and merge, and log requests in a changes list.
Point lookups, apps and flows at the list, filtering on Active and branching on the code.
Record which lists, apps and flows depend on it and review the list quarterly.
commonMistakes: Deleting values that existing items reference.
Flows that branch on the display name.
Everyone on the site being able to edit the list.
No stable code, so renames break integrations.
troubleshooting: If lookups went blank after a delete, restore the row from the recycle bin within 93 days and the links return.
If a retired value disappears from an edit form, include the record's current value in the drop-down's Items.
If unique values cannot be enforced, the column needs an index and must have no existing duplicates.
If test and production IDs differ, match on Code when moving data between sites.

faqs.question: What is a reference list in SharePoint?
faqs.answer: A list of shared values such as departments or categories that other lists, apps and flows look up instead of each keeping its own copy.

faqs.question: Should I delete old reference values?
faqs.answer: No. Mark them inactive so existing items keep their value, and filter new entries to active values.

faqs.question: Why give each reference value a code?
faqs.answer: A code that never changes lets flows, reports and integrations keep working when the display name is renamed.

create-a-metadata-cleanup-view.shortDescription: A set of SharePoint views and a quick-edit routine for finding and fixing items with missing or wrong metadata, grouped so an owner can clear a batch at a time.
create-a-metadata-cleanup-view.fullDescription: A view that lists items with blank metadata shows the size of the problem. A cleanup view goes further: it is arranged for fixing, with the offending columns first, grouping by the person or folder responsible, grid editing enabled and a companion view that proves the backlog is shrinking.
create-a-metadata-cleanup-view.problemStatement: A library has 3,000 documents and a third have no document type or owner. Search refiners and retention labels depend on those columns, and nobody will open 1,000 property panels.
whenToUse: Libraries or lists where key columns were optional or added later
After a migration that brought files in without metadata
Before turning on required columns, retention or metadata navigation
whenNotToUse: Lists over the 5,000 threshold without indexes on the filter columns
Metadata that can be derived by rule, where a flow or script should set it
create-a-metadata-cleanup-view.formulaOrCode:
View 1: "Cleanup: missing metadata"
  Columns (in this order): Type icon, Name, DocType, Owner, ReviewDate, Modified By, Modified, Folder path
  Filter:   DocType is equal to (leave blank)
            OR Owner is equal to (leave blank)
            OR ReviewDate is equal to (leave blank)
  Group by: Modified By   (collapsed)      Sort: Modified descending
  Folders:  Show all items without folders
  Item limit: 100, in batches
  Leaving the value box empty in the filter means "is blank".

Large libraries (over 5,000 items)
  OR filters across several columns cannot use an index. Create one view per column instead, each on an
  indexed column:
    "Cleanup: no DocType"   Filter: DocType is equal to (blank)
    "Cleanup: no Owner"     Filter: Owner is equal to (blank)
  Add the indexes first: Library settings > Indexed columns.

View 2: "Cleanup: suspect values"
  Filter: DocType is equal to "Other"  OR  ReviewDate is less than [Today]
  Catches defaults nobody changed and review dates in the past.

View 3: "Cleanup: progress"
  Filter: none.   Group by: DocType.   Totals: Count on Name.
  The (Blank) group's count is the backlog. Note it weekly.

Highlight what is missing (view formatting on View 1, Format current view > Advanced mode)
  {
    "$schema": "https://developer.microsoft.com/json-schemas/sp/v2/row-formatting.schema.json",
    "additionalRowClass": "=if([$DocType] == '' || [$Owner.title] == '', 'sp-field-severity--warning', '')"
  }

Fix in bulk
  Edit in grid view: type or paste values down a column, fill handle to copy. Esc to cancel a row.
  Multi-select + Details pane: select up to 100 files, open the information pane, set a value once for all.
  Drag to group: in a grouped view, dragging an item to another group sets that column.
  Bulk by rule (PnP PowerShell), when the folder implies the value:
    Connect-PnPOnline -Url https://contoso.sharepoint.com/sites/policies -Interactive
    Get-PnPListItem -List "Documents" -PageSize 500 | Where-Object {
        -not $_["DocType"] -and $_["FileDirRef"] -like "*/Procedures*" } | ForEach-Object {
        Set-PnPListItem -List "Documents" -Identity $_.Id -Values @{ DocType = "Procedure" } -UpdateType SystemUpdate }
    SystemUpdate leaves Modified and Modified By unchanged and adds no version.

Share the work
  Because View 1 groups by Modified By, each contributor can be sent a link filtered to their group:
    .../Forms/Cleanup.aspx?FilterField1=Editor&FilterValue1=Jordan%20Lee
  A weekly flow can count blanks per person and send each a reminder with that link.

Keep it clean afterwards
  When the backlog reaches zero: make the columns required, set column default values per folder
  (Library settings > Column default value settings), and keep View 1 as a monitor. It should stay empty.
stepByStepInstructions: Decide which columns count as required metadata and index them.
Create a cleanup view filtered to blanks, with those columns first and grouping by the responsible person.
Add a suspect-values view and a progress view with counts.
Fix in batches with grid editing, multi-select and scripts where a rule applies.
Send contributors filtered links to their own items.
Make the columns required and set folder defaults once the backlog is cleared.
commonMistakes: One OR filter across unindexed columns on a large library.
Making columns required before cleanup, which blocks every edit on old files.
Fixing by opening one property panel at a time.
No measure of progress.
troubleshooting: If the view shows a threshold error, split it into one view per indexed column.
If grid edit will not save a row, another required column on that row is empty.
If bulk edits flood people with alerts, use a script with a system update.
If blanks keep appearing, set default values per folder and make the column required.

faqs.question: How do I find files with missing metadata in SharePoint?
faqs.answer: Create a view filtered where the column is equal to an empty value, one condition per column you care about.

faqs.question: How do I bulk edit metadata in SharePoint?
faqs.answer: Use Edit in grid view, select several items and edit them in the details pane, or run a PnP PowerShell script.

faqs.question: Can I update metadata without changing Modified By?
faqs.answer: Yes. PnP PowerShell's Set-PnPListItem with UpdateType SystemUpdate keeps the modified date and editor.

create-a-permissions-review-register.shortDescription: A register that records each periodic review of who has access to a SharePoint site: what was checked, by whom, what was removed and when the next review is due.
create-a-permissions-review-register.fullDescription: Auditors ask one question about access: show me that someone reviews it. A permissions review register is the evidence. Each row is one review of one site or library by its owner, with the membership counted, exceptions confirmed or removed, and a next-due date that drives reminders.
create-a-permissions-review-register.problemStatement: Site owners are told to review access annually. Nobody can say which sites were reviewed, what was found or who signed it off, and leavers and old project guests still have access.
whenToUse: Sites holding confidential, personal or regulated content
Tenants with many owner-managed team sites
Organisations with audit or certification requirements for access reviews
whenNotToUse: Group-based access where Entra access reviews are licensed and cover the same membership
A log of one-off permission exceptions, which is a separate register
create-a-permissions-review-register.formulaOrCode:
List: Permissions Review Register (in a governance site)
  Column              Type                    Notes
  Title               Single line             "<Site name> <yyyy>-Q<n>"
  SiteUrl             Hyperlink               Required
  Scope               Choice                  Whole site, Library, Folder
  Sensitivity         Choice                  Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted
  Reviewer            Person                  The site owner doing the review. Required.
  ReviewDue           Date                    Required. Indexed.
  ReviewCompleted     Date
  Status              Choice                  Scheduled, In progress, Complete, Overdue. Indexed.
  OwnersCount         Number
  MembersCount        Number
  VisitorsCount       Number
  GuestsCount         Number
  UniquePermsCount    Number                  Items, folders or libraries with broken inheritance
  SharingLinksCount   Number                  Anyone and organisation links
  RemovedCount        Number                  Users, guests and links removed in this review
  Findings            Multiple lines          What was wrong and what was done
  Evidence            Hyperlink               Exported report stored in the Evidence library
  SignedOff           Yes/No                  Reviewer confirms access is appropriate
  NextReviewDue       Date                    Calculated by the flow from Sensitivity

Review frequency by sensitivity
  Restricted: 3 months     Confidential: 6 months     Internal: 12 months     Public: 12 months

What the reviewer checks (shown as the list form's description, or a linked page)
  1. Owners: at least two, all current staff.
  2. Members and visitors: each person still needs access. Prefer groups to individuals.
  3. Guests: each has a sponsor and a current reason.
  4. Unique permissions: Site settings > Site permissions > Advanced > "Some content has unique permissions".
  5. Sharing links: Site usage > Shared with external users; library > Manage access.
  6. Access requests go to a monitored mailbox or the owners.
  7. Remove what is not needed, record counts, attach the export, tick SignedOff.

Evidence export (admin or owner, PnP PowerShell)
  Connect-PnPOnline -Url $siteUrl -Interactive
  Get-PnPGroup | ForEach-Object {
      $g = $_.Title
      Get-PnPGroupMember -Group $_ | Select-Object @{n="Group";e={$g}}, Title, Email, LoginName
  } | Export-Csv ("access-" + (Get-Date -Format yyyyMMdd) + ".csv") -NoTypeInformation

Views
  Due in 30 days     Status <> Complete AND ReviewDue <= [Today]+30        sorted by ReviewDue
  Overdue            Status <> Complete AND ReviewDue < [Today]
  Completed          Status = Complete, grouped by Sensitivity
  My reviews         Reviewer = [Me]

Automation (scheduled flow, daily)
  1. Get items: ReviewDue le '<today+14>' and Status ne 'Complete'  ->  email the reviewer with the checklist link.
  2. Get items: ReviewDue lt '<today>' and Status ne 'Complete'     ->  set Status Overdue, copy the governance lead.
  3. When an item changes to Complete (separate flow): create the next row with
       ReviewDue = addDays(ReviewCompleted, 90 | 180 | 365 by Sensitivity), Status Scheduled.

Completion rule (list validation)
  =IF([Status]="Complete",AND(NOT(ISBLANK([ReviewCompleted])),[SignedOff]=TRUE),TRUE)
  Message: A completed review needs a completion date and sign-off.

Report for audit
  Completed view filtered to the period, exported to Excel, plus the Evidence library folder for each site.
stepByStepInstructions: Create the register in a governance site with the columns above.
Add one scheduled row per site in scope, with its owner as reviewer and a due date by sensitivity.
Publish the reviewer checklist and the evidence export script.
Add views for due, overdue, completed and each reviewer's own items.
Build flows that remind reviewers, mark overdue items and schedule the next review on completion.
Export completed rows and evidence for audits.
commonMistakes: Recording only that a review happened, with no counts or findings.
Reviewing group membership but not unique permissions and sharing links.
No next-due date, so reviews depend on memory.
Someone other than the owner signing off.
troubleshooting: If owners do not know how to see unique permissions, link the checklist to the site's advanced permissions page.
If reminders go to leavers, check the Reviewer column against active users monthly.
If validation blocks saving, the completion date or sign-off is missing.
If counts are tedious to collect, give owners the export script or run it centrally and attach the file.

faqs.question: What is a permissions review register?
faqs.answer: A list that records each periodic access review of a site: who reviewed it, what they found, what was removed and when the next review is due.

faqs.question: How often should SharePoint permissions be reviewed?
faqs.answer: Commonly every 3 months for restricted content, 6 months for confidential and yearly for the rest.

faqs.question: What evidence do auditors expect from an access review?
faqs.answer: A dated record with the reviewer, the membership checked, changes made, sign-off and an exported membership report.

create-a-launch-readiness-hub.shortDescription: A SharePoint page that gathers everything about an upcoming site or app launch in one place: status, checklist progress, open risks, key dates, owners and communications.
create-a-launch-readiness-hub.fullDescription: Launch information ends up spread across a checklist, an email thread, a Planner board and a slide deck. A readiness hub is one page the whole launch team opens: a status banner, the checklist filtered to what is open, risks, the timeline and the communication drafts. It is built from standard web parts over lists, so it updates itself.
create-a-launch-readiness-hub.problemStatement: In the week before go-live, the sponsor asks whether the launch is on track and gets three different answers, because each workstream tracks its own list.
whenToUse: Launching an intranet, a department site, a business app or a migration wave
Launches with several workstreams and a go or no-go meeting
Repeated launches that should follow the same format
whenNotToUse: A small site change one person can complete in a day
Ongoing operations after launch, which need a support page instead
create-a-launch-readiness-hub.formulaOrCode:
Site: a small team site or a page in the project site. Page: "Launch readiness" (set as home during the launch)

Lists behind the page
  Launch Checklist   Title, Workstream (Content, Permissions, Technical, Training, Comms, Support),
                     Owner, DueDate, Status (Not started, In progress, Done, Blocked), Critical (yes/no), Notes
  Launch Risks       Title, Impact (H/M/L), Likelihood (H/M/L), Owner, Mitigation, Status (Open, Closed)
  Launch Decisions   Title, Decision, DecidedBy, DecidedOn
  Events list or group calendar for key dates

Page layout
  Section 1 (full width): status banner
    Text web part, edited by the launch lead after each stand-up:
    "Status: AMBER. Launch date 14 March. 3 critical items open. Go/no-go: 12 March 10:00."
    Or drive it from a one-row "Launch Status" list shown with a List web part and column formatting.
  Section 2 (three columns): key numbers
    Quick chart or three List web parts with totals:
      Checklist done / total       view "All", Totals: Count, grouped by Status
      Critical items open          view "Critical open"
      Open risks                   view "Open risks"
    Countdown timer web part to the launch date.
  Section 3 (two thirds / one third)
    Left:  List web part: Launch Checklist, view "Open by workstream"
    Right: People web part with the launch lead, sponsor, technical lead, comms lead, support lead
           Quick links: test site, runbook, training material, support channel
  Section 4 (two columns)
    Left:  List web part: Launch Risks, view "Open risks"
    Right: Events web part (next 30 days) and Launch Decisions, newest first
  Section 5: Document library web part filtered to the "Communications" folder (drafts and final messages)

Checklist views
  Open by workstream   Status <> Done, grouped by Workstream, sorted by DueDate
  Critical open        Critical = Yes AND Status <> Done
  Overdue              DueDate < [Today] AND Status <> Done
  Mine                 Owner = [Me] AND Status <> Done

Status pill on the Status column (column formatting, Advanced mode)
  { "$schema": "https://developer.microsoft.com/json-schemas/sp/v2/column-formatting.schema.json",
    "elmType": "div",
    "style": { "padding": "2px 10px", "border-radius": "12px", "display": "inline-block" },
    "attributes": { "class": "=if(@currentField == 'Done', 'sp-css-backgroundColor-successBackground50', if(@currentField == 'Blocked', 'sp-css-backgroundColor-errorBackground50', if(@currentField == 'In progress', 'sp-css-backgroundColor-warningBackground50', 'sp-css-backgroundColor-neutralBackground20')))" },
    "txtContent": "@currentField" }

Go/no-go rule (written on the page)
  GO when: no critical checklist items open, no high-impact risks open without an accepted mitigation,
  support rota confirmed, rollback steps tested.
  The decision and who made it are recorded in Launch Decisions.

Keep it alive
  Daily in launch week: owners update their items before the stand-up, the lead updates the banner after.
  A scheduled flow posts the "Critical open" and "Overdue" counts to the launch channel each morning.

After launch
  Change the banner to the hypercare status for two weeks, then archive: move the page out of navigation,
  set the lists to read-only and save the site as a template for the next launch.
stepByStepInstructions: Create the checklist, risks and decisions lists with owners and due dates.
Build views for open, critical, overdue and personal items.
Lay out the page with a status banner, key numbers, the open checklist, people, risks and dates.
Format the status column so blocked and done items stand out.
Write the go or no-go rule on the page and record the decision in the decisions list.
Update daily in launch week, then archive the hub and keep it as a template.
commonMistakes: A hub that needs manual copying from other trackers.
No single owner for the status banner.
Showing all checklist items so the open ones are buried.
Leaving the hub in navigation long after launch.
troubleshooting: If web parts show the wrong items, check each one is set to the intended view.
If totals are missing in a web part, add Totals to the view and reselect it.
If team members cannot update items, give them edit rights on the lists, not just the page.
If the countdown is wrong for remote teams, state the time zone beside it.

faqs.question: What is a launch readiness hub?
faqs.answer: A single SharePoint page showing launch status, open checklist items, risks, dates, owners and communications, drawn from lists.

faqs.question: Which web parts suit a launch page?
faqs.answer: List web parts with filtered views, a countdown timer, People, Quick links, Events and a document library for communications.

faqs.question: How do I decide go or no-go?
faqs.answer: Agree a written rule in advance, such as no critical items open and support confirmed, and record the decision and who made it.

create-a-site-lifecycle-review.shortDescription: A yearly review that decides whether each SharePoint site should be kept, archived or deleted, using activity, ownership and content facts, with the outcome recorded.
create-a-site-lifecycle-review.fullDescription: Sites are easy to create and rarely closed. A lifecycle review asks, once a year for every site, whether it is still used, who owns it and what should happen to it. The inputs come from the admin centre's activity data, the decision comes from the owner, and the outcome is recorded so that archiving and deletion are deliberate.
create-a-site-lifecycle-review.problemStatement: A tenant has 2,400 sites. Half have had no activity in a year, 300 have no active owner, storage is nearly full and search results are full of old project sites.
whenToUse: Tenants with self-service site or team creation
Storage, Copilot readiness or search quality concerns caused by old sites
Organisations needing a defensible process for deleting content
whenNotToUse: Reviewing who has access, which is the permissions review
Retention of records, which is set by retention policies and labels, not owner choice
create-a-site-lifecycle-review.formulaOrCode:
Inputs (SharePoint admin centre > Active sites, export to CSV; or PowerShell)
  Connect-PnPOnline -Url https://contoso-admin.sharepoint.com -Interactive
  Get-PnPTenantSite -Detailed | Select-Object Url, Title, Template, StorageUsageCurrent,
      LastContentModifiedDate, Owner, GroupId, SharingCapability, LockState |
      Export-Csv sites.csv -NoTypeInformation
  Add from the Microsoft 365 usage report (SharePoint site usage): page views, active files, last activity date.
  Group-connected sites: owners come from the Microsoft 365 group (Get-PnPMicrosoft365Group -IncludeOwners).

List: Site Lifecycle Register
  Title (site name), SiteUrl, SiteType (Team, Communication, Channel, Classic), Purpose (Project, Department,
  Community, Records), PrimaryOwner (person), SecondaryOwner (person), Created, LastActivity (date),
  StorageGB (number), Sensitivity (choice), RetentionLabelled (yes/no),
  ReviewDue (date), Recommendation (choice: Keep, Archive, Delete, Investigate),
  OwnerDecision (choice: Keep, Archive, Delete), DecisionReason, DecidedOn, ActionStatus (Pending, Done), ActionDate

Triage rules (set Recommendation before asking the owner)
  No activity for 12 months and no retention label          -> Archive
  No activity for 24 months, project type, no records       -> Delete (after archive period)
  No active owner                                           -> Investigate: assign an owner first
  Active in the last 90 days                                -> Keep
  Fewer than 5 files and older than 6 months                -> Delete (never really used)

Owner questions (email or form, one per site)
  1. Is this site still needed? (Yes, in use / Yes, reference only / No)
  2. Who are the two owners for the next year?
  3. Does it hold anything that must be kept (contracts, records, HR, legal)?
  4. If no longer active: archive (read-only, kept) or delete?
  No reply after two reminders (14 and 28 days): the site follows the Recommendation and its manager is told.

Outcomes
  Keep      Confirm owners, set ReviewDue + 12 months.
  Archive   Microsoft 365 Archive (admin centre > Active sites > Archive) where licensed: site goes offline to
            cold storage and can be reactivated. Otherwise: set the site read-only
            (Set-PnPTenantSite -Identity $url -LockState ReadOnly), remove from hub navigation, add "(Archived)"
            to the title, and review again in 12 months.
  Delete    Confirm no retention hold. Delete the site (or the group for group-connected sites).
            It stays in the recycle bin for 93 days. Record the date.

Built-in help
  Site lifecycle management policies (SharePoint Advanced Management) can detect inactive sites and email
  owners automatically. Microsoft 365 group expiration policy does the same for group-connected sites.
  Use the register for decisions and exceptions those policies do not capture.

Views
  Due this quarter | No owner | Recommended archive | Awaiting owner | Actions pending | Completed this year

Yearly cycle
  Month 1: export and triage.   Month 2: owner decisions.   Month 3: act and report:
  sites reviewed, kept, archived, deleted, storage freed, sites with no owner resolved.
stepByStepInstructions: Export site, storage, owner and activity data from the admin centre.
Load it into a lifecycle register and apply the triage rules to set a recommendation.
Fix sites with no active owner before asking for decisions.
Ask each owner the four questions and record the decision and reason.
Keep, archive or delete according to the outcome, checking retention first.
Report the results and schedule next year's review date for kept sites.
commonMistakes: Deleting on inactivity alone without checking retention or asking the owner.
Treating no reply as approval without a stated rule.
Archiving sites but leaving them in navigation and search.
Skipping ownerless sites because nobody answers.
troubleshooting: If last activity looks wrong, compare the content modified date with the usage report, since views do not change it.
If a site cannot be deleted, a retention policy or hold applies. Record it as kept under retention.
If an owner has left, use the manager or the group's remaining owners to assign a new one.
If a deleted site is needed, restore it from the admin centre's deleted sites within 93 days.

faqs.question: How do I find inactive SharePoint sites?
faqs.answer: Export Active sites from the SharePoint admin centre and sort by last activity, or use the site usage report in the Microsoft 365 admin centre.

faqs.question: Should inactive sites be archived or deleted?
faqs.answer: Archive when content may be needed or must be kept, delete when the site was never really used or holds nothing of value, after checking retention.

faqs.question: How long can a deleted SharePoint site be restored?
faqs.answer: For 93 days from the deleted sites page in the SharePoint admin centre.

create-a-content-owner-register.shortDescription: A SharePoint list that names an accountable owner and a backup for every site, library and key page, with a confirmation date, so questions and reviews always have somewhere to go.
create-a-content-owner-register.fullDescription: Content without an owner goes stale and nobody can approve its removal. A content owner register maps each significant piece of content to a person, a backup and a business area, and asks them to confirm it periodically. Review reminders, page footers and support routing all read from it.
create-a-content-owner-register.problemStatement: A policy page is wrong. The author left two years ago, the site has six owners who each think someone else maintains it, and the service desk has no idea who to ask.
whenToUse: Intranets and knowledge sites with many pages and libraries
Before starting content reviews, migrations or a Copilot rollout
Organisations where ownership is by role and people move often
whenNotToUse: Small team sites where the two site owners own everything
Recording who has permission, which the permissions review covers
create-a-content-owner-register.formulaOrCode:
List: Content Owner Register (governance or intranet site)
  Column            Type                Notes
  Title             Single line         Name of the content: "HR Policies library", "Expenses page"
  ContentUrl        Hyperlink           Required. Enforce one row per URL by convention plus a duplicate check flow.
  ContentType       Choice              Site, Library, List, Page, Document set, News category
  BusinessArea      Choice or lookup    Department that is accountable
  Owner             Person              Accountable for accuracy. Required. One person, not a group.
  BackupOwner       Person              Required.
  OwnerRole         Single line         Job role, so the entry survives a change of person: "Head of Payroll"
  Audience          Choice              All staff, Department, Managers, External
  ReviewCycle       Choice              3 months, 6 months, 12 months
  LastConfirmed     Date                When the owner last confirmed ownership
  NextConfirmation  Calculated          =IF(ISBLANK([LastConfirmed]),[Created],[LastConfirmed])+365
  Status            Choice              Active, Owner needed, Retiring, Retired
  Notes             Multiple lines

Indexes: Owner, Status, BusinessArea.          Versioning on.
Permissions: everyone can read (people need to find the owner). Governance team edits.
Owners confirm through a flow or a small form, not direct edit.

Views
  By business area     Grouped by BusinessArea, Status = Active
  Owner needed         Status = Owner needed            (the work queue)
  Confirmation due     NextConfirmation <= [Today]+30 AND Status = Active
  My content           Owner = [Me] OR BackupOwner = [Me]
  Retiring             Status = Retiring

Build the first version
  1. Export site pages and libraries (PnP PowerShell):
       Get-PnPListItem -List "Site Pages" -PageSize 500 |
         Select-Object @{n="Title";e={$_["Title"]}}, @{n="Url";e={$_["FileRef"]}},
                       @{n="Author";e={$_["Author"].Email}}, @{n="Modified";e={$_["Modified"]}}
       Get-PnPList | Where-Object { -not $_.Hidden -and $_.BaseTemplate -in 100,101 } | Select-Object Title, DefaultViewUrl
  2. Register sites and libraries first, then the 50 most-viewed pages (Site usage), then the rest by area.
  3. Propose an owner from the business area, not the last editor, and ask them to confirm.

Confirmation flow (scheduled weekly)
  Get items where NextConfirmation is within 30 days and Status is Active.
  For each: send an adaptive card or email to the Owner:
     "Are you still the owner of <Title>?"   [Yes, still mine]   [No, pass to ...]   [This can be retired]
  Yes   -> update LastConfirmed to today.
  No    -> set Status "Owner needed", notify the governance team with the suggested name.
  Retire-> set Status "Retiring", start the retirement steps.
  No answer after 14 days -> ask the BackupOwner. After 28 days -> Status "Owner needed".

Leaver check (scheduled monthly)
  For each Active row: Office 365 Users "Get user profile (V2)" for Owner.
  If the call fails or accountEnabled is false -> promote the BackupOwner note, set Status "Owner needed",
  tell the business area lead.

Use the register
  Page footer or property: "Content owner: <name>. Last reviewed: <date>" (page property or a List properties web part).
  Service desk: lookup by URL to route content questions.
  Content reviews, retirement and migration plans: owner comes from this list.
  Report: count of Active rows with Status "Owner needed" per business area, monthly.
stepByStepInstructions: Create the register with URL, content type, business area, owner, backup and confirmation columns.
Export sites, libraries and top pages and load them as rows.
Propose an owner per row from the accountable business area and get confirmation.
Add views for owner needed, confirmation due and each person's own content.
Run a confirmation flow on a cycle and a monthly check for owners who have left.
Show the owner on pages and use the register for support and reviews.
commonMistakes: Recording a group or team as the owner.
Using the last editor as the owner without asking.
Building the register once and never confirming it.
Restricting read access so staff cannot find an owner.
troubleshooting: If the same URL appears twice, add a flow that checks for an existing row before creating one.
If owners ignore confirmation requests, escalate to the backup and then the business area lead.
If the calculated next date shows 1900 values, guard the formula with ISBLANK as shown.
If registering every page is too much, register libraries and top pages first.

faqs.question: What is a content owner register?
faqs.answer: A list mapping each site, library and key page to an accountable person and backup, with a date they last confirmed ownership.

faqs.question: Who should own intranet content?
faqs.answer: A named person in the business area accountable for its accuracy, with a backup, not the person who happened to publish it.

faqs.question: How do I keep content ownership current?
faqs.answer: Ask owners to confirm on a cycle and check monthly for owners whose accounts have been disabled.

create-a-hub-navigation-review.shortDescription: A structured review of a SharePoint hub's navigation: every link checked for a working target, an owner, audience and usage, then the menu trimmed and reordered.
create-a-hub-navigation-review.fullDescription: Hub navigation grows by request: each team adds a link and none are removed. A navigation review lists every hub and site link, tests it, checks whether anyone clicks it and who asked for it, then rebuilds the menu around what staff look for. Run it twice a year and after any reorganisation.
create-a-hub-navigation-review.problemStatement: The hub menu has nine top-level items and sixty links. Several lead to deleted sites, two labels mean the same thing, and staff use search because the menu is quicker to ignore than to read.
whenToUse: Hubs older than a year or with more than about 30 links
After a reorganisation, migration or site clean-up
Before launching a redesigned intranet home
whenNotToUse: A new hub whose navigation is still being designed, which needs card sorting first
Local site navigation on a single team site with a handful of links
create-a-hub-navigation-review.formulaOrCode:
1. Inventory the links
   Hub navigation is stored on the hub site. Export it (PnP PowerShell):
     Connect-PnPOnline -Url https://contoso.sharepoint.com/sites/intranet -Interactive
     function Get-Nav($nodes, $level, $parent) {
       foreach ($n in $nodes) {
         [pscustomobject]@{ Level = $level; Parent = $parent; Title = $n.Title; Url = $n.Url; Id = $n.Id }
         $children = Get-PnPNavigationNode -Id $n.Id | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Children
         if ($children) { Get-Nav $children ($level + 1) $n.Title }
       }
     }
     Get-Nav (Get-PnPNavigationNode -Location TopNavigationBar) 1 "" | Export-Csv hubnav.csv -NoTypeInformation
   Also list the associated sites:  Get-PnPHubSiteChild -Identity https://contoso.sharepoint.com/sites/intranet

2. Review sheet (list "Hub Navigation Review" or the CSV in Excel)
   Level | Parent | Label | Url | Works? | Target type | Audience | Owner | Views (90 d) | Duplicate of | Decision | New label | New position
   Decision values: Keep, Rename, Move, Merge, Remove

3. Checks per link
   Works        Open it signed in as a normal member, not as an admin. Note 404, access denied, redirect.
                Script the first pass:
                  Import-Csv hubnav.csv | Where-Object Url | ForEach-Object {
                    try { $r = Invoke-WebRequest -Uri $_.Url -Method Head -UseDefaultCredentials -MaximumRedirection 0 -ErrorAction Stop; $code = $r.StatusCode }
                    catch { $code = $_.Exception.Response.StatusCode.value__ }
                    [pscustomobject]@{ Title = $_.Title; Url = $_.Url; Status = $code } }
                Authenticated SharePoint pages often need a browser check, so treat the script as a filter.
   Audience     Who is it for? Links for one team belong on that team's site. Consider audience targeting
                (Edit navigation > enable audience targeting) for role-specific links.
   Owner        From the content owner register. No owner means a candidate for removal.
   Usage        Target site > Site usage (page views, 90 days). Hub home > Site usage for the hub itself.
   Label        Plain words staff use, 1 to 3 words, no acronyms or team names. Sentence case.
   Duplicates   Same target twice, or two labels for one topic.

4. Design rules for the new menu
   Top level: 5 to 7 items, organised by task or topic, not by org chart.
   Depth: two levels by default (mega menu for three). Each group 4 to 8 links.
   Order: most used first, or alphabetical where there is no clear order.
   External links are marked and open in a new tab only when leaving Microsoft 365.
   Every link target is a site or page with an owner.

5. Validate before changing
   Tree test with 8 to 10 staff: give five tasks ("Where would you claim expenses?") and note the first click.
   Rename or regroup anything that half of them miss.

6. Apply
   Hub site > Edit (on the hub navigation bar): reorder, rename, remove. Save.
   Changes can take time to appear for all users because hub navigation is cached.
   Keep the old export as the rollback copy.

7. Record
   Review date, reviewer, links before and after, removed links with reason, next review date (6 months).
   Tell site owners whose links were removed or renamed before the change goes live.
stepByStepInstructions: Export the hub navigation and the list of associated sites.
Check each link for a working target, audience, owner, usage and duplicate labels.
Decide to keep, rename, move, merge or remove each link.
Draft the new menu with 5 to 7 top-level items grouped by task or topic.
Test the draft with a few staff using short find-it tasks.
Apply the changes, keep the old export, and record the review and next date.
commonMistakes: Testing links as an admin who can open everything.
Organising the menu by department structure.
Adding links on request without an owner or review date.
Removing links without telling the site owners.
troubleshooting: If changes do not appear, wait for the hub navigation cache or check in a private browser window.
If some users see fewer links, audience targeting is on for those nodes.
If a link gives access denied to members, fix the target's permissions or remove the link.
If the script reports 401 or 403 for everything, check links in the browser instead.

faqs.question: How many items should hub navigation have?
faqs.answer: Five to seven top-level items, with four to eight links in each group, is a workable limit.

faqs.question: How do I export SharePoint hub navigation?
faqs.answer: Use PnP PowerShell's Get-PnPNavigationNode on the hub site and walk the child nodes.

faqs.question: How often should hub navigation be reviewed?
faqs.answer: Twice a year, and after any reorganisation or site clean-up.

create-an-external-sharing-exception-pro.shortDescription: A request, approval and expiry process for the cases where a site needs more open external sharing than the tenant default allows, with every exception recorded and time-limited.
create-an-external-sharing-exception-pro.fullDescription: A sensible tenant default restricts external sharing, and then a real project needs to work with a supplier. Without a process, admins either refuse or quietly loosen the setting and forget it. An exception process takes a request with a business reason, gets the right approval, applies the narrowest setting that works, and removes it on an agreed date.
create-an-external-sharing-exception-pro.problemStatement: Three sites were opened to anyone links for a bid two years ago. The bid ended, the setting stayed, and files are still reachable by links nobody tracks.
whenToUse: Tenants where the default sharing level is restricted and some sites need more
Supplier, client and partner collaboration on specific sites
Organisations needing evidence of who approved external access
whenNotToUse: Routine guest invitations already allowed by the default policy
A periodic check of existing external users, which is the sharing review
create-an-external-sharing-exception-pro.formulaOrCode:
Baseline (written in the policy)
  Tenant default: New and existing guests (sign-in required). Anyone links off.
  Default site setting: Existing guests only, or Only people in your organisation for sensitive sites.
  An exception is any site set more permissively than its default, or any domain added to an allow list.

Request list: External Sharing Exceptions
  Title               "<Site> - <partner>"
  SiteUrl             Hyperlink. Required.
  RequestedLevel      Choice: Existing guests, New and existing guests, Anyone links
  Partner             Single line. Organisation name.
  PartnerDomains      Single line. e.g. fabrikam.com
  BusinessReason      Multiple lines. Required.
  DataSensitivity     Choice: Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted
  Requester           Person (site owner)
  Sponsor             Person (business lead accountable for the relationship)
  StartDate           Date
  EndDate             Date. Required. Validation: =AND([EndDate]>[StartDate],[EndDate]<=[StartDate]+365)
  Approver            Person
  Decision            Choice: Pending, Approved, Rejected
  Conditions          Multiple lines. e.g. link expiry 30 days, view only, specific library
  Status              Choice: Requested, Active, Expiring, Removed
  AppliedBy / AppliedOn / RemovedOn

Approval rules
  Sensitivity      Existing or new guests            Anyone links
  Public           Site owner + IT                   IT security
  Internal         Sponsor + IT                      IT security + sponsor
  Confidential     Sponsor + information owner       Not allowed
  Restricted       Not allowed                       Not allowed
  Maximum duration: 12 months for guests, 3 months for anyone links. Renewal is a new request.

Flow 1: on new request
  1. Check sensitivity against the table. Auto-reject disallowed combinations with the reason.
  2. Start and wait for an approval (sponsor, then IT).
  3. Approved: create a task for the SharePoint admin with the exact setting to apply.

Apply (admin, PowerShell)
  Connect-PnPOnline -Url https://contoso-admin.sharepoint.com -Interactive
  # Guests with sign-in, limited to the partner's domain
  Set-PnPTenantSite -Identity $siteUrl -SharingCapability ExternalUserSharingOnly -SharingDomainRestrictionMode AllowList -SharingAllowedDomainList "fabrikam.com"
  # Anyone links (only where approved), with expiry and view-only
  Set-PnPTenantSite -Identity $siteUrl -SharingCapability ExternalUserAndGuestSharing -DefaultSharingLinkType Internal -AnonymousLinkExpirationInDays 30 -DefaultLinkPermission View
  Record AppliedBy and AppliedOn, set Status Active, and add a site description note: "External sharing exception until <EndDate>".

Flow 2: daily expiry check
  EndDate within 21 days and Status Active -> Status Expiring; email requester and sponsor: renew or let it end.
  EndDate passed -> task to the admin to remove.

Remove (admin)
  Set-PnPTenantSite -Identity $siteUrl -SharingCapability ExistingExternalUserSharingOnly
  # or Disabled for sensitive sites
  Then remove guests who no longer need access and delete remaining sharing links
  (site > Site usage > Shared with external users; library > Manage access).
  Record RemovedOn, set Status Removed, tell the owner.

Monthly reconciliation
  Get-PnPTenantSite | Where-Object { $_.SharingCapability -in "ExternalUserSharingOnly","ExternalUserAndGuestSharing" } |
      Select-Object Url, SharingCapability
  Every site in that output must have an Active row in the register. Anything else is investigated and reset.

Views: Pending approval | Active by end date | Expiring | Removed this year | Anyone-link exceptions
stepByStepInstructions: Write the baseline sharing settings and what counts as an exception.
Create the exceptions list with reason, sensitivity, sponsor and a required end date.
Define who approves each combination of sensitivity and sharing level.
Build a flow that rejects disallowed requests, collects approvals and tasks the admin.
Apply the narrowest setting, with domain limits and link expiry, and record it.
Check expiry daily, remove on the end date and reconcile site settings against the register monthly.
commonMistakes: Exceptions with no end date.
Opening the whole site when one library or a domain allow list would do.
Approval by IT alone with no business sponsor.
Never comparing actual site settings with the register.
troubleshooting: If a site setting will not apply, the tenant level is more restrictive. A site cannot exceed the tenant setting.
If guests still have access after removal, delete their site permissions and existing links as well as changing the setting.
If owners miss expiry emails, send them to the sponsor too and post in the site's team.
If reconciliation finds unregistered sites, reset them and ask the owner to raise a request.

faqs.question: How do I allow external sharing on one SharePoint site only?
faqs.answer: Keep the tenant default restrictive and raise the sharing level for that site in the admin centre or with Set-PnPTenantSite, ideally limited to named domains.

faqs.question: Should external sharing exceptions expire?
faqs.answer: Yes. Give each an end date, remind the owner before it and reset the site when it passes.

faqs.question: Can a site be more open than the tenant setting?
faqs.answer: No. A site's sharing level can match or be stricter than the tenant level, never looser.

create-a-list-schema-review-board.shortDescription: A lightweight review board, run from a SharePoint list, that checks proposed changes to shared list schemas before they are made: new columns, type changes, renames and deletions.
create-a-list-schema-review-board.fullDescription: Once apps, flows and reports depend on a list, a column change is a release. A schema review board is a fifteen-minute weekly check where proposed changes are logged, their impact on consumers is assessed and they are approved, adjusted or declined. The board is a list with a few views and a short set of rules.
create-a-list-schema-review-board.problemStatement: Someone renames a column and changes another from text to choice. The canvas app shows errors, a flow fails on a missing field and a Power BI refresh breaks, all discovered by users.
whenToUse: Lists used by a canvas app, flows, reports or integrations
Several people with design rights on the same site
Production lists where downtime matters
whenNotToUse: Personal or single-team lists with no dependants
New lists still in design, where a design review is the right step
create-a-list-schema-review-board.formulaOrCode:
List: Schema Change Requests
  Title             What is changing, e.g. "Requests: add Region column"
  TargetList        Lookup or text: the list affected
  ChangeType        Choice: Add column, Change type, Rename display name, Change choices, Make required,
                            Add index, Delete column, New content type, View change, Validation rule
  Detail            Multiple lines: column name, internal name, type, default, choices
  Reason            Multiple lines
  Requester         Person
  Consumers         Multiple lines: apps, flows, reports, integrations that use this list (from the register)
  Impact            Choice: None, Low, Medium, High
  ImpactNotes       Multiple lines
  TestedIn          Choice: Not tested, Dev copy, Test site
  Decision          Choice: Pending, Approved, Approved with conditions, Declined
  Conditions        Multiple lines
  ReviewedBy        Person (multi)
  ReviewDate        Date
  PlannedDate       Date
  Status            Choice: Proposed, In review, Approved, Done, Declined
  RollbackPlan      Multiple lines

Risk guide (shown on the form)
  Change                               Typical impact   Why
  Add optional column                  None or Low      Consumers ignore it until used
  Add required column                  High             Existing forms and flows that create items fail
  Rename display name                  Low              Internal name is unchanged. Power Apps shows the new name
                                                        after a data refresh; formulas using the old display name
                                                        need updating.
  Change column type                   High             Usually means a new column plus data copy. Breaks formulas,
                                                        flow dynamic content and report types.
  Add or rename choice values          Medium           Flows and formulas that compare text values break on rename
  Delete column                        High             Anything referencing it fails. Data is lost.
  Add index                            Low              Do it before the list passes 5,000 items
  Add validation rule                  Medium           Flows writing values that fail the rule start to error
  Lookup to another list               Medium           Counts toward the 12 lookup-type columns per view limit

Review questions (the board asks these in order)
  1. What depends on this list? Check the consumer register for apps, flows, reports and exports.
  2. Is there a lower-risk way? (optional instead of required, new column instead of type change,
     retire a choice instead of renaming it)
  3. Was it tried on a copy of the list with the app and flows pointed at it?
  4. Who updates each consumer, and when, relative to the change?
  5. How is it undone?
  6. Who tells users, if they will notice?

Board rules
  Members: list owner, app maker, flow owner, a site admin. Quorum: owner plus one consumer.
  Cadence: weekly, 15 minutes. Low-impact items can be approved in the channel between meetings.
  Emergency fixes: make the change, log it the same day, review at the next meeting.
  Nothing rated High goes ahead without a tested copy and a rollback plan.

Views
  This week's agenda    Status = Proposed OR In review, sorted by Impact
  Approved, not done    Status = Approved, sorted by PlannedDate
  History by list       Grouped by TargetList
  Board layout          Group by Status in a Board view to drag items between columns

After the change
  Requester sets Status Done, records the date and confirms each consumer was checked:
  app opened and saved, flows run once, report refreshed.
