   Default         Personal productivity, Microsoft 365     Exists already    Yes         Yes       System
                   integrations. Nothing business-critical.
   Developer       One per maker, for learning and          Any maker         Yes         Optional  System
                   building. Not for sharing with users.
   Team sandbox    Shared build and test for a team or      By request        Yes         Yes       System, 7 days
                   project (Dev, Test).
   Production      Live apps and flows for a business area. By request,       Yes         Yes       System, 28 days
                                                            approved
   Trial           Evaluate a feature for 30 days.          By request        Yes         No        None

2. Where does my work go?
   If you are...                                              Use
   Learning, trying an idea, building a first version         Your Developer environment
   Automating your own mailbox, files or Teams                Default
   Building something others will use                         Team Dev -> Test -> Production, in a solution
   Building with premium connectors or Dataverse              A team or production environment with licences checked
   Handling confidential or regulated data                    A dedicated production environment with its own
                                                              security group and DLP policy
   Supplier or consultant building for us                     A project Dev environment; they never own Production

3. Requesting an environment
   Form: "New environment request" (link). You provide: purpose, business owner, technical owner,
   data sensitivity, expected users, connectors needed, end date for project environments.
   Approval: platform team within 3 working days. Production also needs the business owner's director.
   You receive: the environment URL, the security group to manage access, the DLP policy that applies.

4. Naming
   <Area>-<Purpose>-<Stage>      Finance-Invoicing-Dev, Finance-Invoicing-Test, Finance-Invoicing-Prod
   Developer environments: "<Name>'s Environment" (default naming).
   Region: all environments are created in the tenant's home region unless data residency requires otherwise.

5. Access and roles
   Each team and production environment has a security group. Only members can be added as users.
   Role                     Dev             Test                 Production
   Environment Maker        Makers          Makers               Nobody (deployments only)
   System Customizer        Lead maker      No                   No
   System Administrator     Platform team   Platform team        Platform team + service principal
   App users                Makers          Testers              Business users via groups
   Makers do not edit in Production. Changes arrive as managed solutions through the pipeline.

6. Data policies (DLP)
   Default environment: Microsoft 365 connectors only in the Business group. HTTP and custom connectors blocked.
   Developer and team environments: standard policy, with premium connectors allowed on request.
   Production: policy tailored to the solution's connectors. Requests for changes go through the connector review.

7. Solutions and deployment
   Everything shared is built in a solution with the team's publisher.
   Dev -> Test -> Prod through Power Platform pipelines (or the Azure DevOps or GitHub pipeline for larger teams).
   Connection references and environment variables are set per stage.

8. Capacity and licences
   Each environment with Dataverse uses at least 1 GB of database capacity.
   Requests are checked against available capacity. Production owners review storage quarterly.
   Premium features need Power Apps Premium or per-app licences for each user.

9. Lifecycle
   Developer environments unused for 90 days: owner asked to confirm or delete.
   Project environments have an end date. At that date: extend with a reason, or back up and delete.
   Production environments are reviewed yearly with the business owner.
   Deleted environments can be recovered for 7 days (production: longer under the tenant's policy).

10. Getting help
   Questions: Makers channel.    Requests: the forms linked above.    Incidents: service desk, "Power Platform".

Appendix: current environments (link to the environment inventory)
stepByStepInstructions: Agree the environment strategy and the types you will offer.
Write the types table and a plain decision table for where work belongs.
Describe how to request an environment, who approves and what the requester receives.
Document naming, security groups, roles per stage and the DLP policy for each type.
State the solution, deployment, capacity and lifecycle rules.
Publish the guide, link it from the welcome email and request form, and review it twice a year.
commonMistakes: A strategy that exists only as a diagram.
No decision table, so makers still have to ask.
Rules with no request route to follow them.
Never updating the guide as policies change.
troubleshooting: If makers keep using the default environment, link the guide from the welcome email and restrict default-environment connectors.
If requests stall, publish the approval time and who approves.
If the guide and reality differ, link to the live inventory instead of listing environments in the text.
If makers cannot create developer environments, check the tenant setting that controls who can create them.

faqs.question: What should an environment strategy guide contain?
faqs.answer: The environment types, a decision table for where work goes, how to request one, naming, roles, DLP, deployment, capacity and lifecycle rules.

faqs.question: Where should makers build Power Apps?
faqs.answer: In a developer environment for learning and first versions, and in team Dev, Test and Production environments for anything shared.

faqs.question: Should makers have edit access in production?
faqs.answer: No. Production changes should arrive as managed solutions through a pipeline, with maker roles limited to development.

create-a-data-loss-prevention-policy-che.shortDescription: A checklist for creating or changing a Power Platform DLP policy: scope, connector classification, the default group, endpoint rules, impact testing and communication, in the order to do them.
create-a-data-loss-prevention-policy-che.fullDescription: A DLP policy change can switch off hundreds of apps and flows at save. The checklist makes each policy change a small project: confirm the scope, classify connectors deliberately, set where new connectors land, check which existing resources would be affected, tell makers before enforcing, and record the decision. It applies to a first policy and to every later edit.
create-a-data-loss-prevention-policy-che.problemStatement: An admin moves a connector to Blocked on a Friday. On Monday forty flows are suspended, makers do not know why, and there is no record of who agreed the change.
whenToUse: Creating the first tenant or environment DLP policies
Any change to connector groups, scope or endpoint rules
Periodic review of existing policies
whenNotToUse: Explaining what the connector groups mean, which is a concept page
Approving a single connector request, which is the connector review process
create-a-data-loss-prevention-policy-che.formulaOrCode:
DLP POLICY CHECKLIST        Policy: ____________   Change: new / edit   Requested by: ________   Date: ________

A. Purpose and scope
[ ] The risk this policy addresses is written in one sentence
[ ] Scope chosen: all environments / all except listed / only listed
[ ] Tenant-wide baseline exists and this policy does not accidentally loosen it
    (when several policies apply to an environment, the most restrictive combination wins)
[ ] Default environment is covered by the strictest policy
[ ] New environments are covered automatically (an "all except" policy catches them)

B. Connector classification
[ ] Business group: connectors allowed to share data with each other (Microsoft 365, Dataverse, approved line-of-business)
[ ] Non-business group: allowed, but cannot be combined with Business connectors in one app or flow
[ ] Blocked: not usable at all. Note that some Microsoft connectors cannot be blocked.
[ ] HTTP, HTTP with Microsoft Entra ID and HTTP webhook considered explicitly
[ ] Custom connectors: pattern rules set (URL patterns to allow or block), with * as the last rule
[ ] Default group for new connectors set (Non-business or Blocked, never Business)
[ ] Each premium or third-party connector in Business has a recorded owner and reason

C. Fine-grained rules (where used)
[ ] Connector action control: specific actions blocked (for example, delete operations)
[ ] Endpoint filtering: allowed or denied endpoints for HTTP, SQL Server, SharePoint, Dataverse, custom
[ ] Desktop flow action groups classified, if desktop flows are in use

D. Impact check before saving
[ ] Inventory exported: apps and flows per environment with their connectors
        Get-AdminPowerApp / Get-AdminFlow, or the CoE inventory
[ ] Resources that combine connectors across the proposed groups are listed
[ ] Resources using connectors proposed as Blocked are listed
[ ] Owners of affected resources identified, with a count per owner
[ ] Exceptions decided: move the resource, change the design, or adjust the policy
[ ] Policy tried first on a sandbox environment containing copies of affected resources

E. Communication
[ ] Notice sent to affected owners at least 10 working days before enforcement:
    what is changing, which of their apps and flows are affected, what to do, who to ask
[ ] Makers channel post and guide updated
[ ] Tenant setting "Customize policy violation message" (governance error message) points to the guide
    and a contact address:  Set-PowerAppDlpErrorSettings -TenantId <id> -ErrorSettings @{ ErrorMessageDetails = @{
        enabled = $true; url = "https://contoso.sharepoint.com/sites/makers/dlp" }; ContactDetails = @{
        enabled = $true; email = "powerplatform@contoso.com" } }
[ ] Service desk briefed on the symptom: flows suspended, apps showing a policy error

F. Apply
[ ] Change made in the Power Platform admin centre > Security > Data and privacy > Data policies
    (or scripted: New-DlpPolicy / Set-DlpPolicy, with the policy JSON kept in source control)
[ ] Enforcement checked: DLP is evaluated when an app or flow is saved or run; existing flows that violate are suspended
[ ] Policy export saved as the new baseline:  Get-DlpPolicy | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 10 > dlp-<date>.json

G. After the change
[ ] Suspended flows and failing apps reviewed after 24 hours and after one week
[ ] Affected owners confirmed fixed, moved or retired
[ ] Decision record completed: what, why, who approved, impact count, exceptions granted with expiry
[ ] Next review date set (6 months)

Approval
Security or compliance lead ____________    Platform owner ____________    Date ________

Common classification starting point
  Business:      SharePoint, Office 365 Outlook, Office 365 Users, Teams, OneDrive for Business, Dataverse,
                 Approvals, Excel Online (Business), Planner, Forms, Notifications
  Non-business:  Consumer services (Outlook.com, OneDrive personal, social media, Gmail, Dropbox)
  Blocked:       Anything not reviewed, where the tenant allows blocking
stepByStepInstructions: Write the risk the policy addresses and choose its environment scope.
Classify connectors into Business, Non-business and Blocked and set the default group for new connectors.
Add action and endpoint rules where a connector needs to be limited, not removed.
Export the app and flow inventory and list every resource the change would break.
Tell affected owners in advance and set the policy violation message.
Apply the change, save the policy export, review suspended flows and record the decision.
commonMistakes: Saving a policy change without checking what it breaks.
Leaving the default group for new connectors as Business.
Forgetting the default environment.
No notice to makers, so the first sign is a suspended flow.
troubleshooting: If flows are suspended after a change, either move the connector back, or have owners redesign and turn the flows on again.
If a connector cannot be blocked, it is one of the non-blockable Microsoft connectors. Limit it with endpoint filtering where supported.
If two policies conflict, remember the most restrictive result applies across all policies on the environment.
If makers see a generic error, configure the policy violation message with a link and contact.

faqs.question: What should I check before changing a DLP policy?
faqs.answer: The scope, connector groups, default group for new connectors, and which existing apps and flows would violate the new policy.

faqs.question: What happens to flows that violate a new DLP policy?
faqs.answer: They are suspended, and apps show a policy error when opened or saved, until the design or the policy changes.

faqs.question: Where should new connectors be placed by default?
faqs.answer: In Non-business or Blocked, so a newly released connector cannot share data with business connectors until reviewed.

create-an-orphaned-app-cleanup-process.shortDescription: A monthly process for dealing with apps and flows whose owner has left: detect, contact the users and manager, then reassign, quarantine or delete to a published timetable.
create-an-orphaned-app-cleanup-process.fullDescription: Finding orphaned resources is a script. Deciding what to do with each one is a process. This one runs monthly: the detection output becomes a work queue, each item is triaged by usage and criticality, a new owner is sought through the leaver's manager and the app's users, and anything unclaimed is quarantined and then deleted after a fixed period, with a backup taken first.
create-an-orphaned-app-cleanup-process.problemStatement: A script reports 180 orphaned apps and flows. The list is emailed to the admin team, nobody is sure which matter, and six months later the list is 240.
whenToUse: Tenants with regular staff turnover and many maker-built resources
After running an orphan detection script or the CoE inventory
Before licence or environment clean-up
whenNotToUse: The detection script itself, which is a separate pattern
Reassigning a known leaver's resources during offboarding, which should happen before the account is disabled
create-an-orphaned-app-cleanup-process.formulaOrCode:
Queue: list "Orphaned Resources"
  Title (resource name), ResourceType (App, Flow), ResourceId, Environment, FormerOwner, FormerOwnerManager (person),
  LastModified, LastUsed (date), UsersLast30Days (number), SharedWith (number), Connectors (text),
  Criticality (choice: Unknown, Low, Medium, High), Stage (choice: Detected, Contacted, Claimed, Quarantined,
  Reassigned, Deleted, Kept as exception), NewOwner (person), ContactedOn, QuarantinedOn, DeleteAfter (date),
  BackupLocation (hyperlink), Notes

Monthly timetable
  Day 1     Detect and load the queue (script or CoE). New rows: Stage Detected.
  Day 2     Triage (below).
  Day 3     Contact manager and users. Stage Contacted.
  Day 17    No claim after 14 days: quarantine apps, turn off flows. Stage Quarantined. DeleteAfter = +30 days.
  Day 47    Still unclaimed: back up, delete. Stage Deleted.
  Published in the governance guide so nobody is surprised.

Triage rules
  Used in the last 30 days by more than 5 people, or flows with successful runs this week   -> High: find an owner fast, do not quarantine without one
  Used in the last 90 days                                                                   -> Medium: standard timetable
  Not used for 90 days, or never shared                                                     -> Low: skip contact, quarantine now, delete in 30 days
  In the default environment, never shared, under 30 days old when the owner left           -> delete after backup
  Usage: Power Platform admin centre analytics, or CoE "App last launched" and flow run history.

Contact message (to the former owner's manager and, for shared apps, the users)
  Subject: Action needed: "<App name>" has no owner
  "<Former owner> owned the Power App '<App name>', used by <n> people in the last 30 days.
   It now has no owner, so nobody can fix or update it.
   By <date + 14 days> please either: nominate a new owner (reply with a name), or tell us it is no longer needed.
   With no reply, the app will be made unavailable on <date> and deleted on <date + 30 days>."
  Send with a flow from the queue (button or Stage change), recording ContactedOn.

Reassign (Claimed)
  Apps:   Set-AdminPowerAppOwner -AppName <id> -EnvironmentName <env> -AppOwner <new owner object id>
  Flows:  Set-AdminFlowOwnerRole -EnvironmentName <env> -FlowName <id> -PrincipalType User -PrincipalObjectId <id> -RoleName CanEdit
          Solution-aware flows: change the owner on the flow's details page or the Dataverse workflow row.
  Then the new owner must: replace connections that used the leaver's account, add a second owner,
  and confirm data source permissions. Stage Reassigned only when a test run or launch works.

Quarantine (unclaimed)
  Apps:   Set-AppAsQuarantined -EnvironmentName <env> -AppName <id>
          Users see a message that the app is unavailable; co-owners and admins can still open it in Studio.
  Flows:  Disable-AdminFlow -EnvironmentName <env> -FlowName <id>
  Quarantine is the test: if someone needs it, they will ask within days. Reverse with
  Set-AppAsUnquarantined / Enable-AdminFlow once an owner is named.

Back up before deleting
  Apps:   export the package from the admin centre, or for solution apps export the solution.
          Canvas app: Details > Export package (.zip) stored in the "Retired apps" library.
  Flows:  Export > Package (.zip), or solution export.
  Record BackupLocation. Keep for 12 months.

Delete
  Remove-AdminPowerApp -EnvironmentName <env> -AppName <id>
  Remove-AdminFlow -EnvironmentName <env> -FlowName <id>
  Deleted canvas apps can be recovered for a limited time with Get-AdminDeletedPowerAppsList and
  Get-AdminRecoverDeletedPowerApp. Do not rely on it: keep the export.

Exceptions
  "Kept as exception" needs a named business sponsor, a reason and a review date. An exception with no
  technical owner is still a risk and is listed in the monthly report.

Monthly report
  Detected, claimed, quarantined, deleted, exceptions. Median days from detected to resolved.
  Queue size trend: it should fall.

Prevention
  Offboarding step: HR leaver notice triggers a flow that lists the leaver's apps and flows for the manager
  two weeks before the last day, so reassignment happens while the maker can still explain them.
stepByStepInstructions: Load the detection results into a queue with usage and sharing facts.
Triage each item as high, medium or low using recent usage.
Contact the former owner's manager and the app's users with a clear deadline.
Reassign claimed resources and have the new owner repair connections and add a second owner.
Quarantine unclaimed apps and turn off unclaimed flows after 14 days.
Back up and delete after a further 30 days, record exceptions and report monthly.
commonMistakes: Producing the orphan list and stopping there.
Deleting without a backup or warning.
Reassigning ownership without fixing the leaver's connections.
Quarantining a heavily used app before finding an owner.
troubleshooting: If the owner cannot be set, check you are using the new owner's object ID and that they have access to the environment.
If a reassigned flow still fails, its connections belong to the disabled account. Recreate them under the new owner.
If users complain after quarantine, unquarantine once an owner is named, not before.
If the queue keeps growing, add the offboarding step so resources are reassigned before the account is disabled.

faqs.question: What is an orphaned Power App?
faqs.answer: An app whose owner's account has been disabled or deleted, leaving nobody able to edit or maintain it.

faqs.question: What should I do with orphaned apps and flows?
faqs.answer: Triage by usage, ask the former owner's manager and users to nominate a new owner, then reassign, or quarantine and later delete what nobody claims.

faqs.question: Should I delete orphaned apps straight away?
faqs.answer: No. Quarantine first, keep an exported backup and delete after a published waiting period.

create-a-portal-table-permission-model.shortDescription: A design document for Power Pages table permissions: a matrix of web roles against tables with access type and privileges, parent and child chains, and test cases, agreed before anything is configured.
create-a-portal-table-permission-model.fullDescription: Table permissions decide what each site visitor can see and change. Configuring them one by one in the studio, without a model, leads to gaps and to Global access granted to make an error go away. A permission model is drawn first: for each table, which web role gets which access type and privileges, how child tables inherit through relationships, and how each rule will be tested.
create-a-portal-table-permission-model.problemStatement: A partner portal goes live with a Global read permission on Cases added during a late fix. Partners can see each other's cases, and nobody can say which permission was meant to apply.
whenToUse: Any Power Pages site with signed-in users and more than two or three tables
Sites with customers, partners or suppliers who must see only their own data
Before a security review or go-live
whenNotToUse: The click-by-click configuration of one permission, which is covered separately
A fully public information site that exposes no Dataverse data
create-a-portal-table-permission-model.formulaOrCode:
1. Roles (who)
   Web role                Assigned to                              Notes
   Anonymous Users         Everyone not signed in (built in)        Keep to public reference data only
   Authenticated Users     Every signed-in contact (built in)       Baseline for all members
   Customer                Contacts of customer accounts            Sees own records
   Customer Admin          Nominated contact per account            Sees all records for their account
   Partner                 Contacts of partner accounts             Sees cases assigned to their account
   Staff Reviewer          Internal users signing in to the site    Broad read, limited write

2. Access types (how rows are scoped)
   Global    All rows of the table. Use for reference data and trusted staff roles only.
   Contact   Rows related to the signed-in contact through a named relationship.
   Account   Rows related to the contact's parent account through a named relationship.
   Self      The contact's own contact row.
   Parent    Rows related to a row the user can already reach through another permission (child permission).

3. The matrix (one row per table and role; R read, W write, C create, D delete, A append, AT append to)
   Table              Role             Access    Relationship                 Privileges     Notes
   Product (ref)      Anonymous        Global    -                            R              Public catalogue
   Country (ref)      Authenticated    Global    -                            R              Drop-down source
   Contact            Authenticated    Self      -                            R W            Own profile
   Account            Customer         Account   contact_customer_accounts    R              Own company
   Account            Customer Admin   Account   contact_customer_accounts    R W
   Case               Customer         Contact   incident_customer_contacts   R C AT         Own cases
   Case               Customer Admin   Account   incident_customer_accounts   R C W AT       All company cases
   Case               Partner          Account   new_case_partneraccount      R W AT         Assigned cases
   Case Comment       Customer         Parent    Case -> new_case_comments    R C A          Child of Case (Contact)
   Case Comment       Customer Admin   Parent    Case -> new_case_comments    R C A          Child of Case (Account)
   Note (annotation)  Customer         Parent    Case -> Case_Annotation      R C A          Attachments on own cases
   Case               Staff Reviewer   Global    -                            R W            Internal only

4. Rules of the model
   No table has a permission unless it appears in this matrix.
   Global access is allowed only for reference tables (read) and named staff roles.
   Delete is granted nowhere unless a row explains why.
   Lookups: to set a lookup on create, the role needs Append on the new row's table and Append To on the target.
   Column-level limits are handled with basic and multistep form design and column permission profiles,
   not by hiding fields with JavaScript.
   Every list, form and Web API call has "Enable table permissions" on. Web API tables also need the site
   settings Webapi/<table>/enabled and Webapi/<table>/fields listing only the columns required.
   A user with several web roles gets the union of their permissions. Check combinations.

5. Parent and child chains (draw them)
   Contact (Self)
   Account (Account) --> Case (Account) --> Case Comment (Parent)
                                        --> Note (Parent)
   Contact --> Case (Contact) --> Case Comment (Parent)
   Each arrow names the relationship used. A child permission is created under its parent permission.

6. Test cases (run with test contacts, one per role, in a private browser window)
   #   As                      Do                                               Expect
   1   Anonymous               Open /cases                                      Redirect to sign-in
   2   Customer A1             Open case list                                   Only A1's cases
   3   Customer A1             Open a Company B case by URL (id in query)       Access denied message
   4   Customer A1             Add a comment to own case                        Saved
   5   Customer Admin A        Open case list                                   All Company A cases, none from B
   6   Partner P1              Edit an assigned case                            Saved
   7   Partner P1              GET /_api/incidents (Web API)                    Only assigned cases returned
   8   Customer A1             PATCH another contact's row through the Web API  403
   9   Contact with no role    Open /cases                                      No rows, no error
   Test 3, 7 and 8 matter most: lists hide rows, but direct URLs and the Web API only respect permissions.

7. Review and change
   The matrix lives in source control with the site (or the project library). Any permission added in the studio
   is added to the matrix first. Run the site checker and the test cases before each release.
   Export for comparison: pac pages download, then review the table-permissions folder in the diff.
stepByStepInstructions: List the web roles and who is assigned to each.
For every table the site touches, decide the access type and privileges per role in a matrix.
Name the relationship each Contact, Account and Parent permission uses.
Draw the parent and child chains so inherited access is visible.
Write test cases per role, including direct URL and Web API attempts.
Configure the permissions from the matrix, run the tests and keep the matrix under change control.
commonMistakes: Granting Global access to clear an access error.
Configuring permissions with no written model.
Testing only through lists, never by direct URL or Web API.
Forgetting that multiple web roles combine.
troubleshooting: If a user sees no rows, check the contact has the web role and the relationship named in the permission links their rows.
If creating a child row fails, add Append on the child and Append To on the parent table permission.
If the Web API returns 403, check the Webapi site settings for the table and the fields list.
If a user sees too much, look for a Global permission on any of their roles, including Authenticated Users.

faqs.question: What is a table permission model in Power Pages?
faqs.answer: A matrix of web roles against tables showing the access type, relationship and privileges each role gets, agreed before configuration.

faqs.question: When should I use Global access in Power Pages?
faqs.answer: Only for read access to reference data and for trusted internal roles. Customer data should use Contact, Account or Parent access.

faqs.question: How do I test Power Pages table permissions?
faqs.answer: Sign in as a test contact for each role and try lists, direct record URLs and Web API calls for both allowed and forbidden rows.

create-a-manager-response-card.shortDescription: An adaptive card sent to a person's manager in Teams that asks for a decision with a comment, waits for the response and handles no manager, no answer and out-of-office cases.
create-a-manager-response-card.fullDescription: Asking a manager something from a flow sounds simple: look up the manager, send a card, read the answer. In practice the manager attribute is empty for some staff, managers are away, and a card in the Flow bot chat is easy to miss. This pattern covers the whole exchange: resolving the manager with a fallback, a card designed for a quick decision, a timeout with a reminder and delegate, and writing the response back.
create-a-manager-response-card.problemStatement: A leave request flow sends a card to the requester's manager. For contractors with no manager set, the flow fails. For managers on holiday, the request sits for two weeks.
whenToUse: Leave, expense, access and exception requests needing a line manager's decision
Decisions simple enough for two or three buttons and a comment
Organisations with reliable manager data in Entra for most staff
whenNotToUse: Formal approvals needing reassignment, history and mobile approval centre, where the Approvals connector fits
Decisions by a group, where a channel card is better
create-a-manager-response-card.formulaOrCode:
1. Resolve the manager (Scope "Find manager")
   Office 365 Users: Get manager (V2)   User (UPN): requester's email
   Scope "No manager" (run after Find manager has failed):
     Get item from "Approver Fallbacks" by department, or use a default approver mailbox
   Compose "ApproverEmail":  coalesce(body('Get_manager_(V2)')?['mail'], outputs('Fallback')?['body/Approver/Email'])
   Guard: if ApproverEmail equals the requester's email (people who are their own manager in the directory),
          use the fallback.
   Out of office (optional): Office 365 Outlook "Get mail tips for a mailbox (V2)" for the approver.
     If automaticReplies/message is not empty, use the delegate from the fallback list and mention this on the card.

2. Card (Post adaptive card and wait for a response; Post as Flow bot; Post in Chat with Flow bot; Recipient: ApproverEmail)
   {
     "type": "AdaptiveCard", "$schema": "http://adaptivecards.io/schemas/adaptive-card.json", "version": "1.4",
     "body": [
       { "type": "TextBlock", "text": "Decision needed: leave request", "weight": "Bolder", "size": "Medium", "wrap": true },
       { "type": "ColumnSet", "columns": [
         { "type": "Column", "width": "auto", "items": [
           { "type": "Image", "style": "Person", "size": "Small", "url": "@{outputs('PhotoDataUri')}", "altText": "Requester photo" } ] },
         { "type": "Column", "width": "stretch", "items": [
           { "type": "TextBlock", "text": "@{triggerOutputs()?['body/Author/DisplayName']}", "weight": "Bolder", "wrap": true },
           { "type": "TextBlock", "text": "Submitted @{formatDateTime(triggerOutputs()?['body/Created'],'d MMM, HH:mm')}", "isSubtle": true, "spacing": "None", "wrap": true } ] } ] },
       { "type": "FactSet", "facts": [
         { "title": "Type", "value": "@{triggerOutputs()?['body/LeaveType/Value']}" },
         { "title": "Dates", "value": "@{formatDateTime(triggerOutputs()?['body/StartDate'],'d MMM')} to @{formatDateTime(triggerOutputs()?['body/EndDate'],'d MMM yyyy')}" },
         { "title": "Working days", "value": "@{triggerOutputs()?['body/Days']}" },
         { "title": "Balance after", "value": "@{sub(triggerOutputs()?['body/Balance'], triggerOutputs()?['body/Days'])} days" } ] },
       { "type": "TextBlock", "text": "@{triggerOutputs()?['body/Reason']}", "wrap": true },
       { "type": "Input.Text", "id": "comment", "label": "Comment", "isMultiline": true, "maxLength": 500 },
       { "type": "Input.Text", "id": "rejectReason", "label": "Reason (required to decline)", "isVisible": false }
     ],
     "actions": [
       { "type": "Action.Submit", "title": "Approve", "style": "positive", "data": { "decision": "Approved" } },
       { "type": "Action.Submit", "title": "Decline", "style": "destructive", "data": { "decision": "Declined" } },
       { "type": "Action.Submit", "title": "Ask a question", "data": { "decision": "Query" } },
       { "type": "Action.OpenUrl", "title": "Open request", "url": "@{triggerOutputs()?['body/{Link}']}" }
     ]
   }
   Update message: "Thanks, your response has been recorded."        Timeout (action settings): P3D

3. Read the response (run after: is successful)
   Decision:  body('Post_card')?['data']?['decision']
   Comment:   body('Post_card')?['data']?['comment']
   Responder: body('Post_card')?['responder']?['displayName'] and ?['email']
   Condition: decision is 'Declined' and comment is empty
     -> post the card again with the text "Please add a reason for declining" (loop with Do until, maximum 2 tries)
   Switch on decision:
     Approved -> Update item: Status Approved, DecisionBy, DecisionOn, ManagerComment. Notify requester.
     Declined -> Update item: Status Declined with the comment. Notify requester.
     Query    -> Start a chat between manager and requester (Create a chat, then Post message in chat) with the
                 comment, set Status "Query", and send the card again when the requester replies or after 2 days.

4. No response (run after: has timed out)
   Reminder: post a short message in the chat with Flow bot: "Reminder: leave request from <name> is waiting."
   Send the card again with timeout P2D.
   Second timeout -> send to the manager's manager (Get manager V2 again) or the fallback, noting
   "Escalated: no response from <manager> in 5 days", and tell the requester who now has it.

5. Record
   Write to the request: ApproverAsked, AskedOn, ResponseMinutes
   (div(sub(ticks(utcNow()),ticks(outputs('AskedOn'))),600000000)), EscalatedTo.

Notes
  The person photo needs a data URI: Get user photo (V2) then concat('data:image/jpeg;base64,', base64(body('Get_user_photo_(V2)'))).
  Leave the image out when the photo call fails.
  Cards in the Flow bot chat rely on Teams notifications being on. For teams that miss them, also send an
  email with a link, and treat the card as the place to respond.
  Only the recipient can respond to a chat card. For a card several managers can answer, post to a channel.
stepByStepInstructions: Resolve the requester's manager with a fallback for missing or self-referencing manager data.
Optionally check for automatic replies and switch to a delegate.
Post an adaptive card to the manager with the facts, a comment box and decision buttons, with a timeout.
Read the decision and comment and require a reason for a decline.
Update the request and notify the requester for each outcome.
On timeout, remind once, then escalate to the next manager or fallback and record it.
commonMistakes: No fallback when the manager attribute is empty.
No timeout, so runs wait for 30 days.
Declines with no reason captured.
Assuming the manager saw a Flow bot card.
troubleshooting: If Get manager fails, the user has no manager in Entra. Use the fallback scope and report the gap to HR or IT.
If the flow does not continue after the timeout, add has timed out to the next action's run-after.
If the photo breaks the card, send the image as a data URI or remove it.
If the response data is empty, check the input IDs on the card match the names read from the response.

faqs.question: How do I send an adaptive card to someone's manager?
faqs.answer: Use Get manager (V2) for the requester, then Post adaptive card and wait for a response to that manager in a chat with the Flow bot.

faqs.question: What if the user has no manager in Entra?
faqs.answer: Catch the failed lookup and use a fallback approver from a list, such as a department lead.

faqs.question: How do I handle a manager who does not respond?
faqs.answer: Set a timeout on the card action, send a reminder, and escalate to the next manager or a delegate after a second timeout.

create-a-user-mention-notification-patte.shortDescription: A reusable child flow for Teams notifications that mention the right people: it takes recipients, a message and a link, builds the mentions and posts to a chat or channel in one consistent format.
create-a-user-mention-notification-patte.fullDescription: Mentioning a user in a single card is a known recipe. A notification pattern makes it reusable: one child flow that any process calls with a list of emails, a title, body text and a link. It resolves each person, builds the mention entities, chooses chat or channel, avoids notifying the same person twice and returns the message ID so callers can update or reply to it later.
create-a-user-mention-notification-patte.problemStatement: Eight flows each post to Teams differently. Some mention people, some print a name as plain text, one mentions the whole channel, and when the mention format changes every flow has to be edited.
whenToUse: Several flows that notify named people in Teams
Notifications that must reach an assignee and optionally their backup
Teams wanting one look and one place to change notification behaviour
whenNotToUse: A one-off message from a single flow, where a direct action is simpler
Broadcasts to a whole team, which should use a channel post or tag mention sparingly
create-a-user-mention-notification-patte.formulaOrCode:
Child flow (in a solution): "Notify people in Teams"
  Trigger: Manually trigger a flow
    Recipients (Text)    semicolon-separated emails: "ana@contoso.com;raj@contoso.com"
    Title (Text)         Message (Text)        LinkUrl (Text)        LinkText (Text)
    Target (Text)        "chat" or "channel"   TeamId (Text)         ChannelId (Text)
    Severity (Text)      "info", "warning", "urgent"
    ReplyToMessageId (Text, optional)

1. Clean the recipient list
   Compose "Emails":  union(json('[]'), split(toLower(replace(triggerBody()?['text'],' ','')), ';'))
   Filter array "ValidEmails": where item() contains '@'         (removes blanks from trailing semicolons)
   union with an empty array removes duplicates.

2. Resolve people (Apply to each ValidEmails, concurrency 5)
   Scope "Try": Office 365 Users: Get user profile (V2)   User: item()
     Append to varPeople: { "id": "@{body('Get_user_profile_(V2)')?['id']}", "name": "@{body('Get_user_profile_(V2)')?['displayName']}",
                            "upn": "@{body('Get_user_profile_(V2)')?['userPrincipalName']}" }
   Scope "Catch" (run after Try has failed): Append to varUnresolved: item()
   Guests and disabled accounts fail the lookup and are reported, not mentioned.

3. Build the mention parts
   Select "Entities" from varPeople:
     { "type": "mention", "text": "<at>@{item()?['name']}</at>",
       "mentioned": { "id": "@{item()?['upn']}", "name": "@{item()?['name']}" } }
   Select "AtTags" (text mode) from varPeople:  concat('<at>', item()?['name'], '</at>')
   Compose "MentionLine":  join(body('AtTags'), ', ')
   Two people with the same display name need distinct text: append a number to the tag text and the entity text for duplicates.

4. Card
   {
     "type": "AdaptiveCard", "$schema": "http://adaptivecards.io/schemas/adaptive-card.json", "version": "1.4",
     "msteams": { "entities": @{body('Entities')} },
     "body": [
       { "type": "Container", "style": "@{if(equals(triggerBody()?['text_6'],'urgent'),'attention',if(equals(triggerBody()?['text_6'],'warning'),'warning','emphasis'))}",
         "items": [ { "type": "TextBlock", "text": "@{triggerBody()?['text_1']}", "weight": "Bolder", "wrap": true } ] },
       { "type": "TextBlock", "text": "@{outputs('MentionLine')}", "wrap": true },
       { "type": "TextBlock", "text": "@{triggerBody()?['text_2']}", "wrap": true }
     ],
     "actions": [ { "type": "Action.OpenUrl", "title": "@{coalesce(triggerBody()?['text_4'],'Open')}", "url": "@{triggerBody()?['text_3']}" } ]
   }
   Text passed into JSON must be escaped: replace(replace(text, '\', '\\'), '"', '\"'), with line breaks removed or replaced by a space.

5. Post (Switch on Target)
   channel -> Condition: ReplyToMessageId is empty
                Yes: Post card in a chat or channel (Flow bot, Channel, TeamId, ChannelId)
                No:  Reply with adaptive card in a channel (Message ID = ReplyToMessageId)
              Only members of the team receive the mention notification. Others are listed but not notified.
   chat    -> Apply to each person: Post card in a chat or channel (Flow bot, Chat with Flow bot, Recipient = upn)
              A mention is not needed in a one-to-one chat; the chat itself notifies. Leave the mention line out.
              For one group conversation: Create a chat (members = all UPNs joined with ;) then post in that chat.

6. Respond to the caller
   MessageId (Text): body('Post_card')?['id']
   Notified (Number): length(variables('varPeople'))
   Unresolved (Text): join(variables('varUnresolved'), ';')
   Callers store MessageId to reply in the same thread or update the card later.

Rules built into the pattern
  At most 10 people mentioned per message. More than that: mention a tag or post without mentions and link to a view.
  One message per event. Follow-ups are replies in the thread (pass ReplyToMessageId).
  No mentions for "info" severity unless the caller passes exactly one recipient (the assignee).
  Quiet hours: for "info" and "warning", a Delay until 08:00 local time when called outside 08:00 to 18:00.
  The child flow uses embedded connections (run-only users: "Use this connection") so callers need no Teams connection.

Calling it
  Run a Child Flow: Recipients = concat(assigneeEmail, ';', backupEmail), Title = 'Request assigned to you',
    Message = 'REQ-1042: Laptop replacement, due Friday', LinkUrl = item link, Target = 'channel', Severity = 'info'
stepByStepInstructions: Create a child flow with inputs for recipients, title, message, link, target and severity.
Split, lower-case and de-duplicate the recipient emails.
Resolve each person, collecting those that cannot be found.
Build the mention entities and matching at-tags from the resolved people.
Post one card to the channel, a thread reply or individual chats depending on the target.
Return the message ID, the count notified and any unresolved recipients to the caller.
commonMistakes: Building mention JSON separately in every flow.
At-tag text that does not exactly match the entity text.
Mentioning people who are not members of the team.
Unescaped quotes in the message breaking the card JSON.
troubleshooting: If a mention shows as plain text, compare the at-tag in the body with the entity's text character for character.
If the card fails with invalid JSON, escape quotes and line breaks in the title and message inputs.
If someone is not notified, check they are a member of the team that owns the channel.
If the parent cannot call the child, put both in a solution and set the child's connections to embedded.

faqs.question: How do I mention several users in one Teams adaptive card?
faqs.answer: Add a mention entity per person under msteams.entities and include a matching at-tag for each in the card text.

faqs.question: Why make a child flow for Teams notifications?
faqs.answer: One flow holds the mention logic and message format, so every process notifies consistently and changes are made once.

faqs.question: Do mentions notify people outside the team?
faqs.answer: No. Only members of the team receive the notification from a channel mention.
